# START HERE: Google Ranker Pro / Hulk Marketing, 15 real-life videos

**What this pack is.** Everything you need to generate the **raw footage** for 15 short videos on Higgsfield, with copy-and-paste prompts in each video's file.
**Your job:** generate clips with **no text, captions, logos or graphics** in them and send them back.
**Our job:** the edit, which covers the real Search Console and Business Profile receipts, the before-and-after website comparisons, captions, disclosure labels, sound and both ratios.

> Your brief, which every prompt follows: *"It must not feel like AI, CGI, plastic or a 3D game render. It must look like a real-life shot."*

## 3. THE PIPELINE in 7 steps

1. **Consent and photos.** Get written consent covering likeness, voice, approved words, platforms, term and the right to withdraw. Then take **27 photos** with the rear camera, window daylight, a plain wall and no filters or Portrait mode (`research/production_rules.md` A.2). Add 3 front-camera selfies for anyone in a selfie clip (V03, V07, V09, V12, V13's cold open, V14). Record **voice memos**: each approved line separately, 3 takes, 5–8 s, numbers said as words, quiet room, phone about 30 cm away (A.3). Send full-size files, never over WhatsApp. For premises, add 6–10 wide photos.
2. **Character sheet.** Train a **Soul ID** on 20–30 photos and/or make a **Nano Banana Pro** sheet with the B.2 skeleton (3:2, 4k, count 4). Paste the person's wardrobe line verbatim (`pack/characters/`, or `master_plan.md` §3). **No face description, ever.** Build Hassan's sheet from fresh window-light photos, not his studio portraits.
3. **Crops.** Cut the sheet into single views: front head, three-quarter left, three-quarter right, full body front, hands. Attach those, **never the whole grid**.
4. **Anchor still.** **Generate the anchor still first, then animate.** Make one still per set-up with Soul 2.0 or Nano Banana Pro, at the deliverable ratio and in the capture mode's look. A shot needed in both ratios gets two stills. QC each still hard: skin pores, one light direction, no text, green screens showing all four corner dots.
5. **Seedance 2.5.** Paste the prompt from the video file. Attach the @Image references in the order the ASSET MAP lists them. @Audio is used only for a real person's own memo, under 30 s in total.
6. **QC.** Watch every clip at full resolution **with sound** before making the next. Use the checklist in `production_rules.md` §10. Change **one thing** per retry and log it. Never retry silently.
7. **Send back.** See §7 below.

> **Higgsfield settings for every generation**
> - Model **Seedance 2.5** · **Reference** (omni-reference) mode · aspect ratio as the Gen ID says (`16x9` / `9x16`)
> - **1080p, set explicitly every time.** It silently defaults lower. If only 720p is offered, use 720p and tell us; we upscale once in finishing.
> - **Whole-second duration** from the shot list · **Audio on**
> - Selectors: **Era** 2020s · **Physics** realistic · **Tone** calm or warm · **Genre** unset or documentary · **Lens** 24 mm for phone shots, 50 mm (or 85 mm for close-ups) for documentary-camera shots
> - If a selector is set, the prompt never repeats it. Never type a resolution into the prompt.

## 4. REALISM RULES IN ONE BOX

> **The 10 rules that make it look like real footage**
> 1. **One named light source with falloff**, pasted verbatim (window, lamp, street lamp, overcast sky). Name where the shadow falls. No golden hour, no sun, no studio or ring light.
> 2. **One capture mode per video** (DOC-CAM, PHONE-SELFIE or PHONE-REAR). Its **texture line goes last, verbatim**. Never mix two modes in one clip.
> 3. **Atmosphere between lens and subject:** rain on glass, breath in cold air, steam from a mug, drizzle, a smeared windscreen.
> 4. **Lived-in dressing:** two or three anchors that stay put, plus **one uncomposed element** (a crooked blind, a cable on the floor, a half-cropped passer-by, a ticket face-down on the dash).
> 5. **Real physics and weight:** chairs creak, sleeves drag, tea shivers, suspension settles. Every car gets the VEHICLE lock.
> 6. **Behaviour, not emotion:** blinks, glances away, restarts a gesture, rubs the neck, a small nod. Never "looks happy" or "confident".
> 7. **The skin line:** real people get `Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched.`; anonymous hands get pores, fine hairs and one imperfection.
> 8. **Optics match the device:** phones have deep focus and no creamy bokeh; DOC-CAM has a gently soft background. The camera behaves like a hand, a shoulder or a tripod, with no gimbal, drone, dolly or slow motion.
> 9. **Strip the hype:** no cinematic, 8K, ultra-realistic, photorealistic, masterpiece, stunning, flawless, perfect, polished, professional, studio or glossy. No lens brands or ISO. No "no AI look"-style negations.
> 10. **One wet week in October:** paste the palette line for the scene (exterior, interior or car), keep colours muted, add **no readable text anywhere**, and make every screen turned away, soft or flat green with four corner dots.

> **If a clip looks like AI, CGI, plastic or a game render: fix in this order, one change per retry**
> - **Plastic or waxy skin:** strip any hype words → check the person has no face prose → check whether the anchor still was glossy and remake it → only then add `natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, no smoothing.`
> - **Game render** (even light, everything sharp, too clean): name one light source with falloff → add two dressing anchors and one uncomposed element → add atmosphere → add physics lines → as a last resort, put `No game-engine look, no CG gloss.` next to the light line.
> - **Toy-like car:** VEHICLE lock → a real car photo as a prop reference → a shorter shot with the camera static while the car moves.
> - **Floaty motion:** add physics lines, use one action per stage and make the clip shorter. **Gimbal-smooth camera:** paste the handheld line and remove the move words.
> - Full table: `production_rules.md` D.7.

---

## 5. HONESTY IN ONE BOX

> - **Real people come only from their own photos, with written consent.** A generated face attached to a real name or a real quote is a fabricated testimonial, which the DMCC Act 2024 and the CAP Code ban. A face and a voice are also personal data. So: no consent, no clip. Never describe a real person's face, and never generate an "Ali".
> - **Client words:** we send questions, not sentences. The client answers in a voice memo, we transcribe it, they approve it, and only then do their exact words go into the prompt. Until then the prompt shows `[APPROVED LINE n FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT]`. Owners say no numbers; the numbers are ours, on screen with a source. Agency people edit and approve our drafts.
> - **Disclosure labels** (on screen throughout; you and your adviser confirm the final wording):
>   - Real person, re-created: `AI re-creation made with [Name]'s permission. Their words, their voice. Real data.`
>   - Real voice over faceless footage: `Dramatised visuals. Real voice, real data.`
>   - AI presenter (fallback only): `AI presenter. Real client data. Not a client testimonial.`
>   - No-face b-roll: `Illustrative footage. Real data.` (V04: `Dramatised reconstruction · Real data`)
> - **Platform labels on every post:** TikTok AI-generated content (AIGC) toggle, YouTube "altered or synthetic content", Meta "AI info".
> - **No "No.1", "#1", "first", "just hit", "now", growth figures or up-arrows** until there is a dated ranking capture or a Search Console Compare export. 1.8 is said as "top two on average".
> - **Every number** comes from `assets/gsc/gsc_data.json` or a dated capture of a live site. Impressions are "times shown", never "people".
> - **This matches what your site already does:** googlerankerpro.com labels its presenters "AI-generated presenters and voices. Service explanations, not client testimonials."

## 7. HOW TO SEND CLIPS BACK

- **File name:** `grp_vNN_<setup>-<shot>_t<take>_<ratio>.mp4`, for example `grp_v04_P-01_t2_9x16.mp4` or `grp_v01_A-03_t1_16x9.mp4`. For the b-roll bank, use `grp_BR01_t1_16x9.mp4`. V10 adds the person before the shot: `grp_v10_T1_A-01_t1_16x9.mp4`.
- **Variants keep the same pattern, with a letter added to the shot:** `C` for an anonymous (Mode C) twin (`grp_v09_B-01C_t1_9x16.mp4`), `RF` for real footage you film yourself in place of a generated shot (`grp_v04_P-01RF_t1_9x16.mp4`), `x` for an extension (`grp_v02_A-01x_t1_16x9.mp4`), and `a` / `b` for a shot split in two (`grp_v12_A-02a_t1_9x16.mp4`). New real-footage shots with no generated twin use `RF` as the set-up (`grp_v13_RF-01_t1_16x9.mov`). Clips for the shared real-footage list in §6 (RF01–RF08) are named `RF<nn>_<place>_<n>`, for example `RF03_kenilworth_1.mov`. Clips you film keep your phone's own file type (.mov or .mp4).
- Download at the generated resolution (**MOV** where offered).
- Send the **passing takes and the near-misses**. A good first half is still usable.
- Send the **anchor stills** and the **character-sheet crops** as well.
- Add a short note giving the **resolution used** (1080p or 720p) and the **selectors** you set.

**What we do in the edit:** we add the real Search Console and Business Profile receipts (exact crops with source and date) and key them into every green screen. We build the before-and-after website comparisons from real captures only, and add word-timed captions inside the safe zones and the disclosure labels. We lay in the real voice memos and ambience and mix to −14 LUFS for social. Each video is cut in both ratios where the plan calls for it, with one light grade and one upscale route per video.

# Founders: character sheets for F1_HASSAN and F2_SAJID

These are the two real founders of Hulk Marketing Ltd (Companies House 15931335, directors Hassan Pasha and Muhammad Sajid). Both are **Mode B**: their faces come only from their own fresh daylight photos, used with their written consent. Their words are agency drafts that they edit, approve and record in their own voice. Nothing in any prompt describes their faces. **There is no AI founder, ever.** If either of them says no, that part of the plan uses the fallback written below, never a generated stand-in. Hassan carries the founder strand (V10, V13, V14, V15, 23 generations). Sajid is optional (V10 extra clip, V13 two-shot); nothing is generated for him until he signs.

**Never use as references:** the black-background studio portraits, the owner portrait, or the 10 s founder clips on hulkmarketing.co.uk (`hassan.mp4`, `sajid.mp4`). They pull Higgsfield towards a glossy studio portrait, which is the opposite of the documentary look.

**On-screen label for both (added by us in the edit):** `AI re-creation made with [Name]'s permission. Their words, their voice. Real data.`

### 2. Consent: get these in writing before any photo is used

Sign this even though he is a director of the company. The signed form is the record behind the disclosure label and the platform AI-content toggles.

- **Likeness and AI re-creation:** we may train a Higgsfield Soul ID and make Nano Banana Pro character sheets from his photos, and generate video of him in the 23 listed shots (V10, V13, V14, V15), plus, only if triggered, the hands-only fallbacks `v13_H-01_16x9`, `v13_H-01_9x16`, `v13_H-02_16x9` and `v13_H-03_16x9` and the optional two-shot with Sajid `v13_B-05_16x9`, and nothing else without asking again.
- **Voice:** his own voice memos are used as the `@Audio` reference in Seedance and laid in as the final soundtrack. If a lip-sync repair is needed, it uses his real memo. We do not clone or synthesise his voice for new words.
- **Approved words only:** he edits and approves every line in writing before recording, and approves the final cut before it is published. Nothing he has not said and heard goes out.
- **Platforms and placements:** googlerankerpro.com (homepage hero, service pages, Golden Line case study); Hulk Marketing social (Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts); every post carries the on-screen AI label and the platform AI-content setting.
- **Term and storage:** a fixed term (the user sets it, e.g. 24 months, renewable). His photos, Soul ID, sheets and memos are personal data, stored privately and deleted at the end of the term or on request.
- **Withdrawal:** he can withdraw at any time. We take the videos down from our own pages and accounts within an agreed number of days and delete the Soul ID, sheets and memos. Copies that others have already shared cannot be recalled, and the form says so.

### 3. Photo shoot checklist (about 20 minutes on a phone)

**Set-up (2 min)**
- Someone else holds the phone. Use the **rear main camera** and wipe the lens first. Portrait mode, beauty mode, filters and flash all **off**.
- Stand facing a big window at about 45° on an overcast day, in front of a plain mid-tone wall (not white, not green, no posters, nobody else in frame).
- Head-and-shoulders photos at **2x zoom from about 1.5 m**. Full-body photos at **1x from about 3 m**.
- **Avoid:** sunglasses, hats, harsh direct sun, office strip lights on their own, ring lights, coloured LEDs, edits. Use today's haircut and beard. Glasses only if he always wears them, and then in every photo.

**Round 1: DESK outfit, all 27 photos (8 min)** (plain navy crew-neck jumper over a white T-shirt, dark trousers, his own watch)

| # | Shot |
|---|---|
| 1–4 | Head and shoulders, front: neutral, soft natural smile, mid-word as if talking, real laugh |
| 5–8 | Three-quarter left, three-quarter right, profile left, profile right (all neutral) |
| 9–12 | Chin slightly up, chin slightly down, looking off camera left, looking off camera right |
| 13–17 | Waist up: front, three-quarter left, three-quarter right, seated at his real desk, talking with one hand mid-gesture |
| 18–20 | Full body: front, back, three-quarter |
| 21–22 | Hands, backs and palms, **watch on**; holding his phone and holding a mug as he naturally does |
| 23 | Close-up of the jumper's neckline, knit and cuff |
| 24–26 | **Front-camera selfies at arm's length**, sitting at the tip-of-the-week desk: neutral, talking, smiling. He needs these because V14 is a propped front-camera shot. |
| 26b | One front-camera photo with the phone **standing on the desk tripod at chest height** (use the timer), saved as `REF_F1_HASSAN_selfie_tripod.jpg` (V14) |
| 27 | Seated at the real tip-of-the-week desk (window camera-left, orange mug, plant, coat on the chair) |

The room must be his real workspace. If it is a serviced office, it stays a small real room, never dressed up as a big HQ.

### 5. Soul ID training note

- **Train a Soul for Hassan:** yes. He appears in many solo shots (23 generations), which is exactly the case a Soul is for. Ask him first, and train only after the consent form is signed.
- **Training set:** 25 photos, all from this shoot: 15 DESK (#1–20, minus the full-body back and profiles if you are short), 7 SUIT, and the 3 DESK selfies. Leave out hands, the collar close-up and location photos, because they carry no face.
- **Where it works:** a Soul runs only on `soul_2` and `soul_cinematic`, one Soul per generation. Anchor stills: Nano Banana Pro from the crops plus the real place photos (the video file's Step 1). Use a `soul_2` still only after two logged identity-drift retries, and attach the place photo if the Soul 2.0 screen accepts one. Check in the UI whether the Soul also appears as an Element for Seedance. If it does not, use the sheet crops below as `@Image` references.
- **Sheet instead of Soul:** for any frame with a second identity (the optional V13 two-shot with Sajid), and whenever the Soul drifts. In a two-person shot, make each sheet's front and three-quarter crops into **Reference Elements** and build the anchor still on `nano_banana_pro`. Never more than two identities in one generation.
- If the Soul and the sheet disagree on his likeness, his real photos decide. Log which one passed.

### 7. Voice memos

**How to record**
- Use a quiet room with soft furnishings (a lounge or bedroom, not the kitchen). Hold the phone about 30 cm from the mouth, slightly off to one side.
- Use the Voice Memos app on its lossless setting, or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder. Mono, one voice, no music or TV. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take clips, record it again.
- Make **one file per line**, with three takes inside it and a 2-second gap between takes. Each take is 5–8 s, said the way he would say it on the phone to a client, not read out.
- Numbers are spoken as words, exactly as written. **His accent is never described anywhere in text.** The existing founder clips are silent, so every memo is new.
- **File name:** `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_<video>_line<n>.m4a`, for example `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v14_line3.m4a`.

**What to record.** These are agency drafts. Hassan edits them and approves them in writing before recording. Lines marked G7 are recorded only once the Golden Line work log confirms them.

**Rules for the lines.**
- Every number above matches `gsc_data.json`:
  - taxi warwick: 665 times shown, average position 10.7, 0.9% click-through.
  - Airport rows: 5.3, 6.1 and 7.1.
  - kenilworth taxis: 6.7.
  - 665 + 486 + 371 = 1,522, at averages 10.7 to 12.6.
- If he rewords a line, the numbers stay exactly as they are.
- Never "last quarter", "people saw", "No.1", "first", or a causal verb (made, drove, caused).
- If the generated voice does not sound like him, it fails QC. Fix it in the order set out in production_rules G.1.

Log each sheet like this: `QC [date] F1_HASSAN sheet_[desk|suit|coat] t[n] [nano_banana_pro] / Verdict PASS|FAIL / Failure: symptom > broken lock > fix`. Change one thing per retry.

| # | Check | If it fails, first fix (production_rules D.7) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Resemblance:** put the front and both three-quarter panels side by side with his real photos #1, #5 and #6. Someone who knows him would say "that's Hassan" at a glance. | Identity drift: use fewer words about the person (confirm no face prose has crept in), put the identity photos first, and include a three-quarter photo. Then try the Soul (`soul_2`) for anchor stills instead of the sheet. |
| 2 | **Skin not smoothed:** at 100% zoom you can see pores and real texture, with no wax or airbrushing, and he is not de-aged. | Plastic skin: strip any hype words, confirm Mode B, and check the source photos were not shot in beauty mode or Portrait mode. If they were, reshoot them. |
| 3 | **No text or logos** on the jumper, shirt, jacket or coat, and no labels or numbers in the gutters. | Gibberish text: name the clothes as plain (the wardrobe line already says "no logos, no printed text"), then fix the area with a region edit. |
| 4 | **Consistent light:** the same soft light from overhead camera-left on a mid-grey background in all twelve panels, with no black studio background and no hard side light. | Looks like a render: name the one real light source with falloff. Check that no studio portrait or founder clip frame was attached. |
| 5 | **Hands:** five fingers on each hand, natural knuckle creases, and the watch on the same wrist as in his photos. | D.7 has no hands row. Add the HANDS lock (`Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.`), or pick a different one of the 4 variants. |

# Character sheets: the agency team (T1_SEO, T2_REPORTING)

These are the two Hulk Marketing team members who do the work the videos show. **T1** is the SEO specialist and **T2** is the reporting lead. Both are **real people, so both are Mode B**. Their face comes only from their own photos, used with written consent. Their words are agency drafts that they edit and approve. Their voice is their own voice memo. Nobody describes their face in any prompt. Their identity, role, the client work they really did and their location are **not confirmed yet**. You confirm them (master_plan §10, questions 1, 4 and 5) before anything is generated. Work through this file in order for each person: consent, then photos, then the sheet, then crops, then voice memos. Every video prompt that uses them attaches the crop files named in step 6. On screen they always carry the label `AI re-creation made with [Name]'s permission. Their words, their voice. Real data.`

**Before you start, for both people**
- **Settings for every sheet:** Nano Banana Pro · 3:2 · 4k · count 4 (pick the best of the four). On the Higgsfield MCP, load the `character-sheet` workflow first.
- **What a sheet prompt contains:** the B.2 layout, the wardrobe line copied exactly, one skin line and one imperfection. It contains **no description of the face, hair, skin tone, age or build**, because the photos carry all of that.
- **Two identities per frame at most.** The only shot with both of them is `v11_O-04_9x16`.

### 3. Photo shoot (20 minutes on a phone, at their real desk)

**Set-up (2 minutes)**

- **Distance:** heads at **2× from about 1.5 m**; full body at **1× from about 3 m**.
- **Light:** window daylight at about 45°, or open shade. **If T2 is in Pakistan, never shoot in direct sun.** Shoot indoors by a window, in open shade, or in the early morning, because harsh sun ruins both skin texture and the Soul.
- **Background:** a plain mid-tone wall, not white and not green, with no posters, no text and nobody else in frame.

**How to record** (production_rules A.3):

- **Delivery:** speak as you would on the phone to a client.
- **Accent:** use their own natural accent. It is never described in text and never changed.

# Warwickshire client owners: character sheets for CLIENT_GOLDENLINE_OWNER, CLIENT_COVENTRY_OWNER and CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER

These are three real taxi-firm owners: Golden Line Taxis (Warwick), Coventry Airport Taxis 247 and Leam Taxis (Leamington Spa). None of them is named publicly, so we have no names yet. All three are **Mode B**. Each face comes only from that owner's own fresh daylight photos, used with his written consent, and **no prompt ever describes a face**. Each owner's words come from his own voice memos. We send questions, he answers, we transcribe, and he approves the exact lines. Until he approves, every prompt carries `[APPROVED LINE n FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT]`. Golden Line and Coventry quote **no numbers**. The numbers are ours, shown on screen with a source. The only exception is the Leam owner in V03, who may say "a hundred and fourteen" and "twenty-five", worded exactly as the receipt and only after Gate G3 passes. **Never generate an "Ali"**, and never use the duplicated "Ali" reviews (Sarah Byrd, Louise Jones), which appear on both Golden Line and Coventry with the brand swapped. If none of these owners consents, his video uses the fallback written below. A generated face never stands in for him.

**If these three businesses turn out to be one operator group** (Coventry's booking widget runs on Leam Taxis' dispatch system, and Golden Line and Coventry share a phone number and the "Ali" reviews; this is UNVERIFIED), one consenting person may witness for each business. In that case he gets **one** Soul or sheet, and each business keeps its own wardrobe line as a separate outfit (add the suffixes `_goldenline`, `_coventry` and `_leam` to his crops). Each clip names only the business whose data is on screen, and the caption says exactly how the businesses connect, for example "Owner, Leam Taxis and Golden Line Taxis".

**Never use as references:** Golden Line's homepage hero (it looks AI-generated, with an invented "Historic Village of Warwick" sign and an invented plate); the York template images reused on Golden Line; Coventry's stock headset operator and stock Mercedes cut-outs; Leam Taxis' yellow-cab theme renders. They are not these men, not their cars and not real UK private hire.

**On-screen label (added by us in the edit):** `AI re-creation made with [Name]'s permission. Their words, their voice. Real data.` V09 uses the same label (V09.md already does).

### 3. Photo shoot checklist (about 20 minutes on a phone)

**Set-up (2 min)**

- Head-and-shoulders photos at **2x zoom from about 1.5 m**. Full-body photos at **1x from about 3 m**.
- **Wear:** his own dark quilted jacket over a plain grey fleece, the exact pieces he will "wear" in V01. If his jacket carries a company logo or hi-vis lettering, use a plain one instead and tell us which.
- **Avoid:** sunglasses, caps or beanies, a hi-vis vest, harsh direct sun, strip lights on their own, any edits. Use today's hair and beard. Glasses only if he always wears them, and then in every photo.

### 7. Voice memos

**How to record**
- Use a quiet room with soft furnishings (a lounge or bedroom, not the kitchen). Hold the phone about 30 cm from the mouth, slightly to one side. No TV, no radio, no dispatch chatter.
- Use the Voice Memos app on its lossless setting, or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder. Mono, one voice. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take clips, record it again.
- **Step 1, the interview:** one relaxed memo of 5 to 10 minutes answering our four questions, said the way he'd tell another driver:
  - Q1 "Before you worked with Hulk, where did your bookings come from, and what was missing?"
  - Q2 "What changed when the new site went live?"
  - Q3 "What's different now, day to day?"
  - Q4 "If another taxi firm asked you about it, what would you tell them?"
  - Q5 (only if the V03 fallback runs): "What are the Kenilworth jobs like for you?"
- **Step 2:** we transcribe it and send him the lines. He approves them in writing.
- **Step 3:** he records each approved line as its own file, with three takes and a 2-second gap between takes. Each take lasts 5 to 8 s.
- His accent is never described anywhere in text.
- **File name:** `MEMO_CLIENT_GOLDENLINE_OWNER_<video>_line<n>.m4a`.

| File | Used in | Line |
|---|---|---|
| `MEMO_CLIENT_GOLDENLINE_OWNER_v01_interview.m4a` | Source only. We also cut V01's 0–6 s opening voice (first sentence of his Q1 answer, over BR01) from it. | Answers to Q1–Q4 |
| `MEMO_CLIENT_GOLDENLINE_OWNER_v01_line1.m4a`, `_line2` | `v01_A-01_16x9` and `v01_A-01_9x16`, at 1 s and 8 s | [APPROVED LINES 1–2 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT, Q1] |
| `MEMO_CLIENT_GOLDENLINE_OWNER_v01_line3.m4a` | `v01_A-02_16x9` at 1 s | [APPROVED LINE 3 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT, Q1] |
| `MEMO_CLIENT_GOLDENLINE_OWNER_v01_line4.m4a`, `_line5` | `v01_A-03_16x9` at 1 s and 8 s | [APPROVED LINES 4–5 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT, Q2]. Only work the G7 work log confirms, for example "the new website". |
| `MEMO_CLIENT_GOLDENLINE_OWNER_v01_line6.m4a` | `v01_A-04_16x9` and `v01_A-04_9x16` at 1 s | [APPROVED LINE 6 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT, Q3]. A second approved Q3 line may run under the receipts as voice only. |

**Rules for his lines:** no numbers, no "number one", "No.1", "first", "now" or "just hit", no review wording and no "Ali". One line per 5–8 s talking stage. If the generated voice does not sound like him, it fails QC. Fix it in the order set out in production_rules G.1.

# Character sheets: York Cars and Organic Fostering (CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER, CLIENT_OF_DIRECTOR)

These are two real clients, each filmed in their own real workplace: the York Cars manager in the yard and dispatch office (V05), and the Organic Fostering director or registered manager at the office table in Beaumont House (V06). Neither business names anyone publicly, so **you ask each client who will appear and how they want to be captioned**. Both are **Mode B**. The face comes only from their own photos, used with written consent. The words are their own answers, transcribed by us and approved by them. The voice is their own voice memo. **No prompt ever describes their face.** Every shot puts the person inside a real place, so the location also comes only from the client's own photos: **no York Cars photos means no V05**, and no Beaumont House photos means V06 runs as the text-only fallback. Work through each person in order: consent, photos, sheet, crops, voice.

**Before you start, for both people**
- **Settings for every sheet:** Nano Banana Pro (`nano_banana_pro`) · 3:2 · 4k · count 4, pick the best of the four. On the Higgsfield MCP, load the `character-sheet` workflow first.
- **What a sheet prompt contains:** the B.2 layout, the wardrobe line copied exactly, one skin line and one imperfection. It contains **no description of the face, hair, skin tone, age or build**.
- **On-screen label (we add it in the edit):** `AI re-creation made with [Name]'s permission. Their words, their voice. Real data.` If the client prefers a role to a name, use the role, e.g. "the operations manager at York Cars".
- **Client words** stay as `[APPROVED LINE n FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT]` until the client approves them in writing. They quote no numbers. All numbers appear on screen in the edit, with their source.

## CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER · York Cars owner or operations manager (real client, name to be confirmed) · Mode B

### 1. Who they are, where they appear, and the fallback

The owner or operations manager of York Cars, a licensed private-hire firm in York. Nobody is named on yorkcars.co.uk, so the client tells you who appears and how they are captioned. On screen they have night-shift energy: a radio earpiece, a lanyard turned round, keys in hand, a jacket damp from the drizzle. They walk us from the wet yard, through the door, into the dispatch room.

| Video | Generation IDs | Outfit |
|---|---|---|
| V05 Night Shift, York | `v05_W-01_16x9`, `v05_W-01_9x16` (yard walk to the door, line 1) | WORK |
| | `v05_W-02_16x9`, `v05_W-02_9x16` (inside the door to the dispatch desk, line 2) | WORK |
| | `v05_B-02_16x9` (opens a car's rear door, presses the child seat's base, shuts it) (only if York Cars confirms in writing that it fits child seats) | WORK |
| **Fallback only** (hands-only consent) | `v05_P-01_16x9`, `v05_P-01_9x16`, `v05_P-02_16x9`, `v05_P-02_9x16` (the POV walk, their own hands only) | WORK (hands and cuffs only) |

`v05_B-01` (the dispatcher's hands) is **not** this person. It is an EXTRA_MODE_C dispatcher, seen only from behind or as hands, and is never presented as the manager or as named staff.

**Fallback if they do not consent**
- **No York Cars photos of the yard and office:** no V05 at all. Generic footage is never presented as York Cars' office or fleet.
- **Photos, but the manager will not appear:** a POV walk-round with only hands in frame, over their real voice memo. The hands are theirs (from their hand photos #21 and #22) only if they sign a hands-only consent. Otherwise no hands appear and the camera simply walks the route. Label: `Dramatised visuals. Real voice, real data.`
- **No voice either:** V05 pauses. No N1 presenter, no stand-in and no generated York staff.

**Rules that never bend:** no 'largest fleet', 'number one', 'Happy Users' or star average; never a York Cars reviewer's name; no livery, roof sign or door lettering unless it comes from their own car photo (every letter checked in QC); cars wait in the yard or at a kerb, never on a rank. Gates G1 (consent), G2 (Hulk's role, since the site footer credits Xoom Media) and G6 (real premises) block this video.

### 2. Consent: get each point in writing, signed before the photos are used

- **Likeness and AI re-creation:** we may make a Nano Banana Pro character sheet (and a Soul ID only if they tick that box) from their photos, and generate the five listed V05 shots of them and nothing else without asking again. Separate tick boxes: (a) full face, (b) hands only, which covers only `v05_P-01_16x9`, `v05_P-01_9x16`, `v05_P-02_16x9` and `v05_P-02_9x16` (the POV walk with their own hands), (c) voice only (no hands of theirs appear).
- **Voice:** their own voice memos are the `@Audio` reference in Seedance and are laid in as the final soundtrack where sync allows. We do not clone their voice or synthesise new words.
- **Approved words only:** they answer our two questions in their own words. They approve the transcribed lines in writing before recording them, and approve the final cut before it is published.
- **The business:** York Cars agrees to its yard, dispatch office and (optionally) one car being photographed and re-created; to being named; and to how Hulk's role is described (the site footer credits Xoom Media). Dispatch screens, customer details and driver details are never photographed.
- **Platforms and placements:** the googlerankerpro.com Local SEO service page (16:9 and 9:16), plus agency social only if they tick that box. Every post carries the on-screen AI label and the platform AI-content setting.
- **Term and storage:** a fixed term (the user sets it, e.g. 24 months, renewable). Photos, sheet, any Soul and the memos are personal data, stored privately and deleted at the end of the term or on request.
- **Withdrawal:** they can withdraw at any time. We take the video down from our pages and accounts within an agreed number of days and delete their assets. Copies already shared by others cannot be recalled, and the form says so.

### 3. Photo shoot checklist (about 20 minutes on a phone)

**Set-up (2 min)**
- Someone else holds the phone. Use the **rear main camera** and wipe the lens. Portrait mode, beauty mode, filters and flash all **off**.
- Shoot **in daylight**, even though V05 is a night film. Use a window at about 45° on an overcast day, or open shade in the yard. Do not shoot at night under the yard lamps or under the office strip lights on their own.
- Use a plain mid-tone wall behind them: not white, not green, no posters, no signage, nobody else in frame.
- Head-and-shoulders photos at **2x zoom from about 1.5 m**. Full body at **1x from about 3 m**.
- **Wear the WORK outfit:** their own dark work jacket over a plain sweatshirt. **If the jacket has a York Cars logo or name on it, cover it with matching tape** or wear a plain one, because the wardrobe line says "no company lettering". The same goes for a hi-vis vest: plain, or the lettering taped over.
- **Take the lanyard and radio earpiece off** for photos #1–20, so the sheet stays clean. They come back in the prop photos below.
- **Avoid:** sunglasses, hats, harsh sun, ring lights, coloured LEDs, edits, and any photo older than about 4 months. Use today's hair and beard. Glasses only if they always wear them, and then in every photo.

**The 27 photos, WORK outfit (10 min)**

| # | Shot |
|---|---|
| 1–4 | Head and shoulders, front: neutral, soft natural smile, mid-word as if talking, real laugh |
| 5–8 | Three-quarter left, three-quarter right, profile left, profile right (all neutral) |
| 9–12 | Chin slightly up, chin slightly down, looking off camera left, looking off camera right |
| 13–17 | Waist up: front, three-quarter left, three-quarter right; **glancing back over the shoulder as if leading someone across the yard** (V05 W-01); talking with one hand mid-gesture |
| 18–20 | Full body: front, **back** (the walk shots are mostly from behind), three-quarter |
| 21–22 | Hands, backs and palms; **holding their real keys** the way they always do |
| 23 | Close-up of the jacket collar, zip and sweatshirt neckline |
| 24–26 | **Skip.** They have no selfie shots. |
| 27 | Standing by the real office door in the yard, in daylight |

**Prop photos (2 min):** the radio earpiece in their ear (note which ear), the lanyard worn with the card turned to face the body (note: card never shown front-on), the keys on their fob or carabiner, and the hi-vis vest if they really wear one in the yard.

**Location photos (6 min; anyone at York Cars can take these):** 6–10 wide photos of each place, from the corners at standing eye height, lights as normal.
- **The yard (L5):** in daylight, plus **2–3 at night with the yard lamps on**, from where the camera will walk, so we know where the lamp really is. Include the walk from the parked cars to the office door, and the door itself.
- **The dispatch office (L5):** radios on chargers, keys on hooks, the kettle, a coat on a chair. **Turn every monitor off or away before you shoot**, because dispatch screens show customer addresses and phone numbers. No rota boards or whiteboards with names in frame.
- **A real car (only if a livery is to appear):** 2–3 photos in daylight from the front three-quarter, side and rear three-quarter. Plates will be hidden in generation.
- Tell us **which address the dispatch office is** (Blossom Street or Unit 2 Heritage Park, YO19 5UP).

**Send:** original full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email at actual size. **Never WhatsApp.** Name the photos `CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER_01.jpg` to `_27.jpg`, and the folders `PHOTOS_CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER_work`, `PHOTOS_CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER_props` and `PHOTOS_L5_yorkcars_[yard|office|car]`.

### 7. Voice memos

**Step 1: the answer memo.** They answer our two questions in their own words, as long as they like, in one file: `MEMO_CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER_v05_interview.m4a`.
- Q1: "What does a Saturday night look like here?"
- Q2: "What do customers ask for most?"

We transcribe it and pick one line per question (5–8 s spoken). **They approve both lines in writing.**

**Step 2: record the approved lines**, one file per line, three takes in each with a 2-second gap.

| File | Shot | Line |
|---|---|---|
| `MEMO_CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER_v05_line1.m4a` | `v05_W-01` (both ratios), at 1 s | [APPROVED LINE 1 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT] |
| `MEMO_CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER_v05_line2.m4a` | `v05_W-02` (both ratios), at 1 s | [APPROVED LINE 2 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT] |

**How to record**
- A quiet room with soft furnishings (not the dispatch room with radios on, not the yard). Phone about 30 cm from the mouth, slightly off to one side.
- Voice Memos on its lossless setting, or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder. Mono, one voice, no radio, music or TV. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS; re-record any take that clips.
- Say it the way they would tell a new driver, not as if reading. A little walking breath is fine; we add the yard and the radio crackle as ambience.
- **What they must not say:** any number, 'largest fleet', 'number one', 'best', a customer's or driver's name, or a review quote. Their accent is never described anywhere in text.
- If the generated voice does not sound like them, it fails QC. Fix it in the order in production_rules G.1.

Log it: `QC [date] CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER sheet_work t[n] [nano_banana_pro] / Verdict PASS|FAIL / Failure: symptom > broken lock > fix`. Change one thing per retry.

| # | Check | If it fails, first fix (production_rules D.7) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Resemblance:** the front and both three-quarter panels, side by side with their real photos #1, #5 and #6. Someone at York Cars would say "that's them" at a glance. | Identity drift: fewer words about the person (confirm no face prose crept in), identity photos attached first, a three-quarter photo included. Then regenerate the sheet from a cleaner set of 3–6 photos. |
| 2 | **Skin not smoothed:** pores and real texture at 100% zoom, no wax or airbrushing, not de-aged, tiredness under the eyes kept if it is in the photos. | Plastic skin: strip any hype words, confirm Mode B, and check the photos were not taken in beauty or Portrait mode. | 3 | **No text or logos** on the jacket, sweatshirt or vest, no lanyard card, and no labels or numbers in the gutters. | Gibberish text: name the clothes as plain (the wardrobe line already says "no logos, no company lettering"), then fix the area with a region edit. |
| 4 | **Consistent light:** the same soft overhead camera-left light on mid-grey in all twelve panels, with no yard-lamp orange, no strip-light green and no hard side light carried over from the photos. | Looks like a render: name the one real light source with falloff; check no night or strip-lit photo was attached. |
| 5 | **Hands:** five fingers on each hand, natural knuckle creases, the hands look like working hands. | D.7 has no hands row. Add the HANDS lock (`Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.`) or pick another of the four variants. |

- **The organisation:** Organic Fostering Ltd agrees, as a regulated agency, to its office being photographed and re-created, to being named, and to Hulk being named as the agency it worked with. The office photos show no carers, no children, no case files and no names.

- **Term and storage:** a fixed term (the user sets it, e.g. 24 months, renewable). Photos, sheet, any Soul and the memos are personal data, stored privately and deleted at the end of the term or on request.

Real tea, steam visible. | A-01 (in hand, set down at about 6 s), A-02 (a sip at 6–8 s), B-01 (steaming in the foreground) |
| Tea level | Fuller in A-01 and B-01, lower after the sip in A-02. The tea is actually drunk, never a prop. | A-01, A-02, B-01 |
| Lanyard | Card turned to face the body in every shot; never readable | All |
| Notebook and pen | One plain notebook with blank pages and one plain pen; nothing written on the page is readable | A-01 (on the table), B-01 |
| The plant | The same plant that needs water, in the same place on the table | A-01, A-02 |
| Watch or ring | Only what they really wear, on the same wrist or finger | All, visible in B-01 |
| Glasses | Only if they really wear them, and then in every shot | All |

### 9. Sheet QC: five checks before cropping

Log it: `QC [date] CLIENT_OF_DIRECTOR sheet_cardigan t[n] [nano_banana_pro] / Verdict PASS|FAIL / Failure: symptom > broken lock > fix`. Change one thing per retry.

| # | Check | If it fails, first fix (production_rules D.7) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Resemblance:** the front and both three-quarter panels, side by side with their real photos #1, #5 and #6. A colleague would say "that's them" at a glance. | Identity drift: fewer words about the person (confirm no face prose crept in), identity photos attached first, a three-quarter photo included. Then regenerate from a cleaner set of 3–6 photos. |
| 2 | **Skin not smoothed:** pores, fine lines and real texture at 100% zoom, no wax or airbrushing, not de-aged or made up beyond their photos. | Plastic skin: strip any hype words, confirm Mode B, and check the photos were not taken in beauty or Portrait mode. If they were, reshoot them. |
| 3 | **No text or logos** on the cardigan or top, the lanyard card turned away in every panel, and no labels or numbers in the gutters. | Gibberish text: name the clothes as plain (the wardrobe line already says "no logos, no printed text"), then fix the area with a region edit. |
| 4 | **Consistent light:** the same soft overhead camera-left light on mid-grey in all twelve panels, with no office-tube green and no window glare carried over from the photos. | Looks like a render: name the one real light source with falloff; check no harshly lit photo was attached. |
| 5 | **Hands:** five fingers on each hand, natural knuckle creases, any ring or watch on the same hand as in the photos. | D.7 has no hands row. Add the HANDS lock (`Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.`) or pick another of the four variants. |

# Character sheets: the AI presenter and the incidental people (N1_AI_PRESENTER, EXTRA_MODE_C)

This file covers the two cast members who are **not real, named people**. **N1** is an invented woman: a clearly labelled AI presenter. She is used **only** if a fallback is triggered in V01 (Version B2: the Golden Line owner takes no part at all) or V15 (Version B: Hassan declines). She is designed once from words (Mode A), you approve her once, and from then on every prompt treats her like a real person (Mode B, no face description). She never quotes a client, never says "we", is never named, and carries `AI presenter. Real client data. Not a client testimonial.` on screen the whole time. **EXTRA_MODE_C** is everyone incidental: a driver's hands on a wheel, a passenger seen from behind, a dispatcher in soft focus. They are nobody, so they are **never identifiable**, never shown with a face, and never presented as a client, a client's driver or customer, or agency staff. They need no sheet and no Soul: two lines of skin and wardrobe (the SKIN-C lock) and one of the six descriptions below. Most of the "make today" shots (BR01, BR02, BR04, V04, V08 and the V11 hands) use them, so get them right first.

**Before you start**
- **Settings for N1's sheet:** Nano Banana Pro · 3:2 · 4k · count 4 (pick the best of the four). On the Higgsfield MCP, load the `character-sheet` workflow first.
- **Make N1 only when a fallback is triggered** (or as an optional test, see `00_START_HERE.md` §2). Her generations are **not** in the 86-take count.
- **No sheet, no Soul, no crops for extras.** Their continuity comes from the anchor still of each set-up and the fixed imperfection in the table in step 8.

---

## N1_AI_PRESENTER · Labelled AI case-study presenter (invented, not a real person) · Mode A once, then Mode B

### 1. Who she is, where she appears, and the fallback

She is an invented woman of about 55: a practical Midlands woman who has run a busy office most of her working life. She is deliberately ordinary, so she is **unlike the five polished GRP service presenters** and the 30 sample portraits on googlerankerpro.com. She sits in a cluttered back room (L10) that is **no particular business**. She tells a real case study in the third person, using real Golden Line data.

| Video | Generation IDs (proposed; fallback only, not in the 86) | What she does |
|---|---|---|
| V01 The Four O'Clock Phone, **Version B2** (the owner takes no part) | `v01_N1-01_16x9` (12 s, medium, lines 1–2), `v01_N1-02_16x9` (10 s, close, line 3), `v01_N1-01_9x16` (12 s, for the 45 s cut) | Introduces Golden Line and hands over to the receipts. The film becomes a **case-study explainer** and is described that way, never as a testimonial |
| V15 What Moved in Warwick, **Version B** (Hassan declines) | `v15_N1-01_16x9` (15 s), `v15_N1-02_16x9` (12 s), `v15_N1-03_16x9` (14 s close), `v15_N1-01_9x16` (15 s), `v15_N1-03_9x16` (14 s) | Narrates the same plates in the third person: "the agency", never "we". **No green screen in her frame.** Her data goes full frame in the edit |

**She is in V01 and V15 only, nowhere else.** She is never in V02–V14. V02, V06, V09, V13 and V14 explicitly forbid an AI narrator.

**If you do not approve an N1** (or would rather not use one):
- **V01:** prefer B1 (the owner's real voice over faceless footage) if he will give a voice memo. If he gives nothing, use A's Leam Taxis film, but only if Gate G3 clears. Otherwise V01 waits.
- **V15:** if Hassan declines and there is no N1, V15 waits. Our suggestion, which needs your OK: a receipts-only explainer over the real Warwick dashcam drive (RF07), with captions and no presenter.
- **Never** swap in a real person's look-alike, a client, or a generated "Ali".

### 2. Approvals and licences (she has no consent form, so get these in writing instead)
- **Your one-time approval of her look:** you sign off the chosen sheet once (date, file name `SHEET_N1_AI_PRESENTER_v1.png`). After that her face is never redesigned, only reused.
- **She is nobody real:** she is built from words only. No real person's photo, no stock photo and no "looks like [name]" was used, and she passes the resemblance check in step 3 (no likeness to the five GRP presenters, the 30 sample portraits, any client, any staff member or any public figure).
- **Voice licence:** her voice is a new synthetic voice designed from the casting brief in step 7, or a stock synthetic voice whose licence allows commercial use with AI disclosure. It is never a clone of anyone. If you hire a human voice actor instead, they sign a consent covering synthetic use, platforms, term and withdrawal.
- **The client's permission:** Golden Line's written permission to be named and to have its Search Console figures shown. This is still needed even though the owner does not appear. "Hulk Marketing built its website" rests on the verified footer credit. Every V15 "what the agency did" line needs the work log (Gate G7).
- **Approved words only:** you approve every line before generation. She speaks in the third person, never says "we", never quotes or paraphrases a client, and says only numbers from `gsc_data.json` with the plan's wording ("times shown", "average", "page one on average", no "No.1", "first", "now" or growth).
- **Labels and platforms:** `AI presenter. Real client data. Not a client testimonial.` stays on screen throughout. The TikTok AIGC, YouTube altered or synthetic and Meta AI-info settings are on for every post. Placement: the Golden Line case study and its social cut. Never the homepage testimonial slot.
- **Term and withdrawal:** keep a list of every published clip she is in. If Golden Line withdraws permission, or anyone says she resembles them, her clips come down within an agreed number of days [7] and she is retired.

### 3. Reference set (she has no photo shoot: about 20 minutes on Higgsfield)

| Step | Time | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 min | Open Nano Banana Pro: 3:2, 4k, count 4. Attach **nothing**. She is made from the words alone |
| 2 | 5 min | Run the sheet prompt (step 4, prompt 1). Pick the one variant out of four that looks most like an ordinary photographed woman, not a model. Save it as `SHEET_N1_AI_PRESENTER_v1.png` |
| 3 | 3 min | Cut the five crops (step 6) from the chosen sheet |
| 4 | 5 min | Run the detail check (prompt 2) with `CROP_N1_AI_PRESENTER_front.png` attached (never the whole sheet). Zoom to 100%: pores, fine lines, the scar's texture and individual brow hairs must be there. Then run the approval still (prompt 3) at 16:9 with the crops attached. She must read as a real woman filmed in a real room |
| 5 | 3 min | **Resemblance check:** put the front crop beside the five GRP service presenters and the 30 sample portraits on googlerankerpro.com. Optional: run the front crop through a reverse image search. Any close likeness to anyone means you regenerate from step 2 |
| 6 | 2 min | Approve, then log it: `APPROVED N1 [date] SHEET_N1_AI_PRESENTER_v1.png`. From now on, **no face prose ever again** |

**Optional location photos for her back room (L10):** 6–10 photos of an ordinary real back room you have permission to use, taken from the corners at standing eye height in overcast daylight. A real room as the location reference makes her clips far less render-like. Clear or turn away anything identifying first: signs, certificates, papers, photos of people, and anything readable through the window. Name the files `LOC_L10_01.jpg` … `LOC_L10_10.jpg`. **Never use a client's premises or the agency room.** She is no particular business.

**Avoid:** uploading any real person's photo, any "in the style of" or "looks like" wording, beauty or skin-smoothing tools, upscaling the sheet, and redesigning her after approval. She never appears in a selfie shot, so she needs no front-camera views.

### 4. Higgsfield prompts

**Prompt 1: the character sheet (Mode A, human-realism 13 blocks).**
Settings: **Nano Banana Pro · 3:2 · 4k · count 4.** No attachments.
Tightened from master_plan §3.2. The broken capillaries are gone, because the age ladder puts them at 70+, not 55. A dry patch by the nostril (the skill's pale-skin cue) replaces them. Her hands are described, so the hands panel holds up. The eye sentence names her iris colour. There is one lived-in clothing detail. The far side of her face gets the light's falloff on three features. Her brows have a few stray hairs but no grey, because the age ladder puts sparse, greying brows at about 65, not 55.

```
Character reference sheet of one invented woman, photographed as twelve equal panels in a 4 by 3 grid with thin plain mid-grey gutters and no labels, no text, no numbers. Row one, head and shoulders at eye level: front facing with a calm neutral expression; three-quarter view turned to her left; three-quarter view turned to her right; left profile. Row two: full body front, head to feet; full body from behind; full body three-quarter view; both hands held up, backs in one and palms in the other. Row three, head and shoulders: a relaxed half-smile; mid-word as if talking, lips slightly parted; thinking, eyes looking just off camera to the left; close-up of the collar and knit of her cardigan. Around 55 years old, a practical woman who has run a busy office most of her working life, but clearly someone who still laughs easily at the end of a long day. White British, fair, warm-toned skin with redness around the nostrils, grey-green eyes, natural brows with a few stray hairs. Chin-length ash-brown hair with grey coming through at the parting, tucked behind one ear, flyaways at the crown and a cowlick at the front hairline. A small pale scar through her left eyebrow. Thin tortoiseshell reading glasses pushed up into her hair. Maximum realism (skin AND hair): moderate wrinkles, horizontal forehead lines, crow's feet, deepening nasolabial folds, faint under-eye hollows with darker circles, early vertical lip lines, a slightly softened jawline, visible pores, uneven pigmentation and mild darker patches, a few sun spots, a small dry patch beside one nostril, peach fuzz along the jaw and upper lip. Do not smooth, soften, rejuvenate or beautify her skin. Detailed grey-green irises with visible fibre texture, natural moisture, tiny visible vessels in the sclera, authentic catchlights. Individual hair strands, eyebrow hairs and eyelashes sharply visible. Her hair looks genuinely grown from the scalp, never painted or artificially perfect. The scar has realistic healed tissue texture and slight tonal variation. Her hands show natural knuckle creases, faint veins and short plain nails, five fingers on each hand. She carries herself plainly and without fuss. No obvious makeup. Wearing a moss-green wool cardigan over a cream crew-neck T-shirt, dark jeans, reading glasses pushed up into her hair; no logos, no printed text, in every panel. The cardigan is a little bobbled at the cuffs; plain flat dark shoes, scuffed at the toes. Seamless neutral mid-grey background (#8C8C8C) in every panel. One large soft light overhead and slightly to camera-left with even soft fill, gentle natural shadow under the chin and nose, the same light in every panel; the far side of her face falls a little darker, with soft shadow in the nasolabial fold, under the cheekbone and beneath the brow. Head panels framed like an 85mm portrait lens, body panels like a 50mm lens, no wide-angle distortion. Fine natural photographic grain.
```

The words "artificially perfect" are part of human-realism's fixed hair sentence (block 11), which tells the model what to avoid. They are not a hype token, so leave them in.

If it comes back glossy or waxy, **remove the sentence "Do not smooth, soften, rejuvenate or beautify her skin." first** (on Nano Banana Pro it can read as noise), then regenerate. Never add hype words to fix it.

**Prompt 2: detail check (optional, 2 minutes).** Nano Banana Pro · 1:1 · 2k · count 1. Attach `CROP_N1_AI_PRESENTER_front.png` only (cut in step 3), never the whole sheet.

```
Extreme close up of her left eyebrow, the small scar through it and her left eye, in this exact position and light. Slight natural imperfections, low exposure.
```

**Prompt 3: approval still (she is now Mode B, no face prose).** Nano Banana Pro · 16:9 · 2k · count 4. Attach `CROP_N1_AI_PRESENTER_front.png`, `_34left.png`, `_34right.png` and `_body.png`, plus `LOC_L10` photos if you took them.

```
The woman in the attached reference images, 100% matching her face, hair, build and proportions, sits at a cluttered desk in a small back room on an overcast late-October afternoon, half-turned towards someone just off camera-left, mid-word, her left hand resting beside a plain cream mug with a tea ring and faint steam rising from it. Wearing a moss-green wool cardigan over a cream crew-neck T-shirt, dark jeans, reading glasses pushed up into her hair; no logos, no printed text. Behind her: a radiator with chipped paint under a window camera-left showing a wet grey yard, box files with blank spines on a shelf, a coat on a hook, a cable trailing across the floor to a socket, a blind hanging slightly crooked. A laptop at the frame edge with its lid angled away. Dust drifts in the window light. Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-left is the only key; the right side of the face falls a stop darker with soft shadow under the cheekbone; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed. Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched. Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated. Her moss-green cardigan stays exactly as in the reference. No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable. Exactly one person visible. No extra people. Filmed on a handheld documentary video camera in available light: natural colour with a restrained grade, fine even digital grain, soft highlight roll-off on bright windows, real depth of field with a gently soft background.
```

The approval still is a test, not a video anchor. Each N1 shot still gets its own anchor still from the video file.

### 5. Soul ID training note
- **Default: no Soul for N1. Use the sheet crops.** She has at most 8 fallback generations, all solo, all in Seedance 2.5, which takes the crops as @Image references. A Soul trained on generated images can also lock in any AI smoothness.
- **Train a Soul only if her anchor stills drift** between set-ups, even with the crops attached. If you do: generate 20–30 varied stills of her on Nano Banana Pro from the crops (front, three-quarters, profiles, waist up, full body; neutral, talking, laughing; her back room by day and by lamp). Keep **only stills that pass the skin check** in step 9, name them `N1_TRAIN_01.png` … `N1_TRAIN_30.png`, and train a Soul named `N1_AI_PRESENTER`.
- **A Soul works only on `soul_2` and `soul_cinematic`.** Use `soul_2` for her anchor stills (the documentary look), with **one Soul per generation**.
- **Multi-person shots use Reference Elements, not a Soul.** She never shares a frame in the plan. If an edit ever puts her beside anyone, that shot uses Elements built from her crops.

### 6. Crops to cut from the sheet

Cut along the gutters so each crop is one panel with no grid lines. Keep the native resolution (no upscaling) and save as PNG. **Attach the crops, never the whole grid.** She has one outfit, so there is no suffix.

**Asset map order:** attach exactly in the "Upload order" list printed above each prompt in V01.md and V15.md; that list decides the @Image numbers (for example `v15_N1-02_16x9` is front, 34right, hands, then its anchor still). **No @Audio** for her (production_rules §C: an invented presenter's prompt describes delivery only).

### 7. Voice: synthetic, labelled, one locked voice

She records no memos, so there are **no `MEMO_` files**. Her voice is designed once and then locked.

**Casting brief** (paste into Higgsfield's voice creation or ElevenLabs Voice Design; three adjectives plus one contradiction, age and region; never "the voice of" anyone):

```
A woman in her mid-fifties from Coventry or Warwickshire, with a soft West Midlands accent. Warm, unhurried and dry, faintly gravelly, plain-spoken but with a hint of a smile in the voice. She talks like someone explaining something useful to a neighbour across a kitchen table: steady pace, short sentences, a small settle at the end of each point. Recorded close in a small quiet room.
```

**How the voice is used**
- Generate 3 auditions and pick one. Save its voice ID as `VOICE_N1_AI_PRESENTER` and never change it.
- Generate each approved line separately: 3 takes, 5–8 s each, numbers written as words. Name the files `VO_N1_AI_PRESENTER_<video>_line<n>_t1.wav` (`_t2`, `_t3`). We keep the best take as `VO_N1_AI_PRESENTER_<video>_line<n>.wav`.
- In Seedance she voices the line from the delivery words only (pace and warmth, not timbre). **In the edit we lay the locked voice in as the final track**, so she sounds identical in every clip. If sync slips, we run a lip-sync repair to the locked voice (production_rules G.1, step 3) and QC it hard.
- **On-screen label, throughout:** `AI presenter. Real client data. Not a client testimonial.` Small, lower-left, above the safe zone. Also mention "AI presenter" in the post text.

### 2. Consent and honesty rules (5 points)
- **Generated extras are nobody, so no consent form is needed. That only holds while they stay unidentifiable:** no face, no tattoo, no distinctive jewellery or watch, and no readable lanyard, name badge or number plate.
- **Never presented as anyone:** not a named client, not a client's driver or customer, not agency staff. Captions never name them. In fallbacks where an owner's real voice plays over Mode C hands, the label reads `Dramatised visuals. Real voice, real data.` and nothing implies the hands are his.
- **Each video's own label stays on:** `Dramatised visuals. Real voice, real data.` (V08); `Illustrative footage. Real data.` (V11 hands, and V06's anonymous `v06_B-01C` hands); `Dramatised reconstruction · Real data` (V04); inside a Mode B film (V01, V02, V05, V12) that film's label covers the BR and Mode C clips, and nothing says the hands are the client's.
- **Never built from a real face:** no client's, driver's, customer's or reviewer's photo, and never a look-alike. Never a generated "Ali".
- **If you use real hands as a reference** (step 3, optional), that person signs a short written OK first: hands only, AI use, the listed videos and platforms, the term, withdrawal by email, and never named or captioned.

### 3. Photo shoot: none needed. Optional real-hands reference (10 minutes)

Generated hands are the weakest part of AI footage. An optional real reference makes them far more convincing. Use only a consenting colleague (or yourself) after the written OK above.

| 3 | Both hands on the lower half of a steering wheel, in a parked car with the engine off, shot from the passenger seat at chest height |

| 8 | Hands typing on a keyboard, sleeves at the wrists |

Cover the badge on the steering wheel with tape. Name them `LOC_L4_car_01.jpg` … `_04.jpg`. It is presented as a reconstruction, not as anyone's car.

**Avoid:** any face in frame, tattoos, rings or a watch with a visible logo, nail varnish or nail art, logos on sleeves, filters, beauty mode, Portrait mode and harsh sun. Nothing makes them look like a client, a driver we know, or staff | **Extra people or a face appears:** state the exact count and "seen only from the chest down", then remove any person from the location still. | 2. Skin not smoothed | Pores, fine hairs, knuckle creases and the one imperfection are visible on the hands. No waxy or rubbery sheen | **Plastic skin:** strip any hype words and check the anchor still was not glossy (remake it if it was). Only then add the earned skin lock |
| 3. No text or logos on clothes | Sleeves, jackets, the case, the lanyard and the keys are plain, and number plates are not readable | **Gibberish text:** paste the TEXT-LOCK, name the object as plain ("a plain dark grey case"), then region-edit or blur it in the edit |
| 4. Consistent light | The hands sit in the set's one named light (L-CAR-DAY, L-TAXI, L-STREET-NIGHT, L-PREMISES or L-OFFICE), with falloff and the same direction as the rest of the shot | **Game-render look:** name the one light source with falloff, add two dressing anchors and one uncomposed element, add atmosphere (rain on glass, steam, breath) |
| 5. Hands | Five fingers on each hand, nothing fused or bent backwards, real weight in every touch (fingertips flatten, the case drags the arm down) | **Floaty or wrong hands:** add the physics (weight, contact, settle), one action per stage, a shorter clip. ---

## What this video is

- **Concept.** A Warwick taxi owner, parked up before sunrise, tells us in his own words what it was like when Google sent no work his way, what changed when the new site went live, and what's different now. Problem (his own car, pre-dawn) → turn (his own back office at dusk, laptop open with a green screen) → result (the real Search Console receipts).
- **Hook.** Black. A wiper thunks once. A phone lights up face-up on a dark dashboard and buzzes against the plastic. Over it, the first sentence of his real answer. No title for 6 s. (9:16: the same image with `312 clicks · 18.2K times shown` on screen by 0.8 s.)
- **Why this brand.** Golden Line is the only client with a verified Hulk credit on its live site (footer: "Made with ❤ by Hulk Marketing Ltd") **and** an attributed Search Console screenshot.
- **What the edit reveals.** At ~37 s the live footer credit is pushed in as proof of the work. At 49 s (65% of the runtime) the real totals land on his laptop's green screen and push to full frame: 312 clicks, 18.2K times shown, 744 different searches, brand searches top two on average (1.8), two airport searches on page one on average. He says no numbers. The numbers are ours, on screen, sourced and dated.
- **The motif.** The film opens and closes on a phone lighting up, its screen never readable.

**Picking lines 6, 6b and 7:** skip any sentence that claims more work, more calls or a before-and-after change ("more", "busier", "up", "doubled") unless he can show his own booking records (G5).

**How he records a memo (send him this):**
- First, one relaxed **interview memo** of 5–10 minutes answering the four questions: `MEMO_CLIENT_GOLDENLINE_OWNER_v01_interview.m4a`.
- After approval, **one approved line per memo**, three takes in the same file with a 2-second gap between takes. Each take must fit its slot: lines 1, 3, 4 and 6 at most 6 s; lines 2, 5 and 7 at most 5 s (line 6b is voice only and can run to 6 s; line 0 is cut from the interview memo). Time each trimmed memo before attaching it. If one runs long, ask for a shorter take; don't stretch the prompt.
- A quiet room with soft furnishings (lounge or bedroom, not the kitchen, not the car with the engine on). No TV, radio or dispatch chatter.
- Phone about **30 cm** from his mouth, slightly to one side (stops pops).
- Voice Memos app on its lossless setting (or any 44.1/48 kHz recorder), mono. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
- Say it the way he'd say it to a customer on the phone, not read out.
- Send the files full size by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. **Not WhatsApp.**
- His accent is never described anywhere. His memo carries his voice.

**If the generated voice doesn't sound like him, it fails QC.** We lay his real memo in as the final track wherever sync allows (production_rules G.1).

29° diagonal field of view, short telephoto portrait lens character, camera 3 to 4 metres from the subject, face sharp, background compressed and softly out of focus, close framing through lens reach, not proximity.

CAMERA
Locked-off on a tripod with the faint micro-movement of a real head. Focus stays on the eyes.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. She takes a small breath in. End state: lips parted, about to speak.
1-8s: At second 1, @Image 1 the presenter says, in natural British English, "These are the last three months, and the positions are averages. There's no earlier period to compare yet.", plain and unhurried, a slight lift of the eyebrows on the second sentence. End state: line finished, eyes on the interviewer.
8-9s: A small nod and a half-smile; her eyes drop briefly to the mug below frame and come back. End state: half-smile, eyes on the interviewer.
9-10s: She holds; ambience only. End state: unchanged, camera holding.

PHYSICS
Her head and shoulders shift slightly with each breath; a few flyaway hairs at the crown move as she nods; the cardigan collar settles against her neck.

LIGHTING
Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-left is the only key; the right side of the face falls a stop darker with soft shadow under the cheekbone; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed.
Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched.

AUDIO
Ambience: a small back-room tone, a radiator ticking, light rain on the window.
Foley: a soft rustle of her cardigan at 8 seconds as she nods.
Dialogue: only the quoted line, spoken by the presenter at second 1, in natural British English; lips still when not speaking; no other voices.
Clean close dialogue as if from a clip-on microphone, natural room tone underneath, no echo.
No background music. No subtitles. At least 1 second of ambience-only before the first word and after the last word.

FINAL FRAME
The presenter in close-up, eyes on the interviewer, a half-smile, camera holding.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated. Her moss-green cardigan stays exactly as in the reference.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
She blinks naturally and glances away to think; fingers do not touch the face during speech.
Exactly one person visible. No extra people.
Filmed on a handheld documentary video camera in available light: natural colour with a restrained grade, fine even digital grain, soft highlight roll-off on bright windows, real depth of field with a gently soft background.

## Edit plan (what we do after hand-back)

**Receipt grammar (every data moment):** the exact crop of the real PNG on a navy `#0B1628` card, 12 px radius; one thin orange `#F7931E` underline under the one figure that matters, with a soft tick; a slow 102% → 108% push-in over 3–4 s with a light grain match; the source line always on (Inter 500, `#BDCBDC`); a context strip where needed. No redraws, no count-ups, no up-arrows, no Google logos or colours on our graphics. Never "No.1", "#1", "first", "just hit", "now", "growth". Never the site's "No.1 Taxi Hire" headline.

**Source line (all Search Console receipts):** `Google Search Console · goldenlinetaxiswarwick.co.uk · 19 Jul–18 Oct 2026`
**Context strip (positions):** `Average position over 3 months. Positions 1–10 are page one.`

## Changes from the master plan (one line each)

- **A-01 phone:** face-down in the tray in front of the gear lever with his mount empty, not "face-down in the dash mount" (a phone can't lie face-down in a mount); it lights up in that same mount in A-05.
- **A-01, A-01_9x16, A-05 lens:** selector 35 mm or unset, because the plan's ~60° field matches neither the 50 nor the 85 mm DOC-CAM block.
- **Faceless shots (BR01, BR02, BR03, B-03, B1):** the light lines drop or re-aim their "face" clause (as master_plan §8.3 does), so the model isn't invited to put a face in frame.
- **BR03:** shot side-on from across the road so the car leaves frame right; driving away from the lens would show its rear plate. It waits for his car photo (attached as @Image 2), since it plays as his car and §2.6 bars a generated client vehicle without the client's photos. For the same reason its TAXI lock names his car's colour and body shape (`A plain dark grey saloon with no livery…`) in place of the lock's "[colour] saloon or people carrier"; the rest of the lock is word for word.
- **BR02 (pre-dawn):** PAL-EXT stays word for word, followed by one night sentence (`Before dawn the low cloud is dark, faintly lit by the town.`), the same way V03 and V05 handle their night exteriors.
- **B-03:** the 47° block at about 70 cm, not 2–3 m, to get the plan's close of a hand.
- **N1 shots:** PAL-INT pasted verbatim plus one line keeping her moss-green cardigan (the palette's "navy, grey and mid-blue" would fight her approved wardrobe); IDs, lines and L-OFFICE light follow `pack/characters/presenter-extras.md`.

## What this video is

- **Concept.** After the last airport run, the owner sits down at his own kitchen table, pulls the laptop in and sees his three months of Google numbers for the first time. T1's **real recorded voice** talks him through it from the laptop speaker. One person on camera; his reactions are cut to the exact moments each number appears.
- **Hook.** 16:9: the keys clatter on the table, he pulls the laptop in, and T1's voice comes out of the speaker: "Right, so this is your last three months on Google." 9:16 duet: the real totals tile (`224 clicks · 15.9K times shown`) is on screen in the top half by 0.8 s; his face leans in below.
- **Why this brand.** Coventry Airport Taxis 247 has a clean, attributed Search Console screenshot with honest airport-search rows: one search averaging page one (7.0), one shown 607 times that is still at 22.0. That lets the film be candid about what's working and what's next.
- **What the edit reveals.** For the first 26 s the data is seen only on his laptop (our real screenshots keyed into the green screen). At about 26 s (59% of the 44 s film) the first receipt goes full frame: `coventry airport taxi · avg 7.0`, page one on average. His own approved line follows. The close is honest: `airport transfers coventry` was shown 607 times but averages 22.0, "so that's the next one".
- **Framing.** "First look at three months", never growth. There is no comparison period (gate G5).

**Deviations from the plan (one line each):**
- The 16:9 runs about 44 s, not 40 s: the receipts and T1's last line need readable holds, and BR04 needs room as the tail. Still inside your 30–45 s format.
- T1's line 4 gains ", on average" ("That's page one, on average"): master_plan §1.5 calls averages of 6–7 "page one on average".
- Row 1's on-screen label reads "the most clicks of any search", not "top search": its average is 13.6 (page two), so "top" could read as a ranking claim.
- In A-01 and V-01 (filmed from behind him) the light line swaps "camera-left" and "camera-right": it is the same bulb and the same window, seen from the other side of the table. Because his face is never seen there, the two colour temperatures meet across the back of his neck and shoulders, not on the face.
- In the reaction shots the plan's GLOW line says "laptop" instead of "phone" (production_rules §E wording for a laptop).
- New, optional: a 6 s extend of A-01 (`v02_A-01x`) to give the edit more clean green-screen time. If you skip it we punch in on A-01 instead.
- New: the voice-only fallback (B2) gets its own IDs (`v02_V-01_16x9`, `v02_V-01_9x16`); the plan names the shots but gave no IDs.
- In the spoken lines the brand is said "Coventry Airport Taxis Twenty-Four Seven" (numbers as words).
- T1's line 3 reads "Most clicks went to airport taxi Coventry: fifteen.", not "Top one's…": that query averages 13.6 (page two), and "top one" is the spoken form of "#1" (G4). `team.md` §7 now carries this wording (and line 4's ", on average").
- In BR04 the LIGHTING clause "soft shadows under the eyes and chin" becomes "soft shadows under the car and the case": no face may be in that shot (as V01's BR03 does).
- The first full-frame receipt (F1) lands at about 26 s, 59% of the 44 s film, a little before the plan's 65–75%: it needs a 2.6 s readable hold before his line at 29 s.

**The owner's line (DRAFT FOR CLIENT APPROVAL).** We send him one question, never a sentence:
> "Which of those searches is the job you want most?"

He answers in a relaxed interview memo (`MEMO_CLIENT_COVENTRY_OWNER_v02_interview.m4a`, 1–3 minutes). We transcribe it and pick one line of 5–6 s. He approves it in writing, then records it on its own: `MEMO_CLIENT_COVENTRY_OWNER_v02_line1.m4a`. In the prompts it appears as `[APPROVED LINE 1 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT]` until then.

|---|---|---|---|
| 29.0–35.0 s | 26.0–32.0 s | v02_A-02 (16:9) / v02_D-02 (9:16), both at his second 1 | [APPROVED LINE 1 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT] |

**Ask him:** no numbers, no "up", "climbing", "doubled", no "No.1" or "first", no review wording, no "Ali". The numbers are T1's and ours, on screen.

**How to record a memo (send this to both of them):**
- One approved line per memo, three takes in the same file with a 2-second gap between takes. Each take 5–8 s.
- A quiet room with soft furnishings (a lounge or bedroom; **not** the kitchen, even though the film is set there). No TV, radio or music.
- Phone about **30 cm** from the mouth, slightly to one side so the breath doesn't pop.
- Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1/48 kHz recorder), mono. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
- Say it the way you'd say it on the phone to a customer, not read out.
- Send full size by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. **Not WhatsApp.**
- Nobody's accent is ever described in a prompt. The memo carries the voice.

**If the generated voice in A-02 or D-02 doesn't sound like him, it fails QC.** We lay his real memo in as the final track wherever sync allows (production_rules G.1). Never ship a voice he hasn't heard and approved.

## Edit plan (what we do after hand-back)

**Receipt grammar (master_plan §1.2):** exact crops of the real PNGs, never redrawn or re-typed, on a navy `#0B1628` card with a 12 px radius; one thin orange `#F7931E` underline under the one figure that matters, with a soft tick; a slow 3–4 s push-in from 102% to 108% with grain matched to the footage. No count-ups, no up-arrows, no Google logos or colours on our graphics.

**Every receipt carries:**
- Source line (Inter 500, `#BDCBDC`): `Google Search Console · coventryairporttaxis247.co.uk · 19 Jul–18 Oct 2026`
- Context strip on every position figure: `Average position over 3 months. Positions 1–10 are page one.`
- On-screen numbers written exactly as the receipts show them: `15.9K`, never "15,900". Impressions are "times shown", never "people".

## What this video is

- **Concept.** At the end of a night shift the owner of Leam Taxis walks from his parked car to his front door, filming himself on his phone's front camera, and says the number in his own words: a hundred and fourteen calls off his Google listing, May to October. At his door he adds the best month: September, twenty-five. Then he turns the key.
- **Hook.** Frame 1 is already his face mid-step, with two short buzzes from a phone in his pocket. The real `114` headline crop is on screen by 0.8 s with its source line, and a 0.6 s flash of his hand slamming the car door gives the first beat.
- **Why this brand.** A running total is the one milestone this data proves without a comparison period: 114 calls made from the Business Profile, May–Oct 2026 (October part month), with September the best of the six months shown at 25 (read exactly from the tooltip). A taxi owner would say that number out loud. It also sets up V09's stitch ("…twenty-five").
- **What the edit reveals.** The real headline crop lands first. The real chart then wipes on left to right above him as he walks (the real pixels revealed, never redrawn). On his word "twenty-five" we punch in on the real September tooltip with the caption `September: 25 calls, the best of the six months shown.` No growth claims, no "first", no "now".

**Changes from the plan (one line each):**
- The pocket buzz moves from second 3 to second 0. The hook needs it on frame 1, and this keeps it out from under his line. It is two short message buzzes, not a ringing call, because a call he ignores breaks the "no call-ignoring" fix (§11).
