## Script and voice memos

**DRAFT FOR CLIENT APPROVAL.** These are line *shapes* only. He rewrites them in his own words and records them, and only his approved words go into Seedance. Until then the prompts carry `[APPROVED LINE 1 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT]` and `[APPROVED LINE 2 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT]`.

**Questions to send him (he answers in one relaxed memo, `MEMO_CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER_v03_interview.m4a`, 1–3 minutes):**
1. "Your Google listing shows a hundred and fourteen calls made from it, May to October. How would you say that to another driver?"
2. "September was the busiest of those six months for calls: twenty-five. How would you put that?"

We transcribe his answers, pick one line for each shot, and he approves them in writing. Then he records each line as its own memo.

| Shot | Starts at (in the clip) | Line shape (he rewrites) | Length | Memo file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v03_S-01_9x16` | second 1 | "A hundred and fourteen calls off our Google listing, May to October." | 5–6 s, ends by second 7 | `MEMO_CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER_v03_line1.m4a` (+ `_outdoor`) |
| `v03_S-02_9x16` | second 1 | "September was the best of the lot. Twenty-five." Then a small laugh (not in the memo) | about 4–5 s, ends by second 6 | `MEMO_CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER_v03_line2.m4a` (+ `_outdoor`) |

**Rules for his lines:**
- The only numbers he may say are "a hundred and fourteen" (May to October) and "twenty-five" (September), said as words, exactly as the receipts show.
- He may not say "first", "now", "just hit", "number one", "best month since May", "since May", "more", "up" or any other growth word. October is a part month, so it is never a drop.
- "Calls", not "customers" or "people": the receipt counts calls made from the profile.
- No review wording and no customer names. No "Hulk did this" or "the agency got us": no causal lines (G2, §1.5).
- If he changes the wording, the numbers stay exactly as they are.

**How to record a memo (send this to him):**
- **Only after G3 clears.**
- One approved line per memo: three takes in the same file, with a 2-second gap between takes. Each take is 5–8 s at most.
- Use a quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a lounge or bedroom (not the kitchen or the car). No TV, radio or music.
- Hold the phone about **30 cm** from your mouth (production_rules A.3), slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop.
- Use Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
- Say it the way you'd tell a mate, not as if you're reading it out.
- **Then record both lines a second time outdoors**, on your phone at arm's length while walking slowly on your street, and save them as `MEMO_CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER_v03_line1_outdoor.m4a` and `..._line2_outdoor.m4a`. These give us the real phone-microphone sound for the final track.
- Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. **Not WhatsApp.**
- Nobody's accent is ever described in a prompt. The memo carries the voice.

**Which memo goes where:** the clean indoor take is the `@Audio 1` reference in Seedance, because it guides timbre and pace best. In the edit we lay in his real voice (`_outdoor` first, or the indoor take with a light phone-mic EQ) wherever sync allows. **If the generated voice doesn't sound like him, that is a QC fail** (production_rules G.1). Never ship a voice he hasn't heard and approved.

| 0.5–1.1 s | `v03_B-01` (clip 1.6–2.2 s): his hand slams the car door | Door thunk |
| 1.1–8.0 s | `v03_S-01` (clip 0.9–7.8 s) | Line 1 (about edit 1.2–6.9 s) |

On a wet late-October night the owner of a small Leamington taxi firm, filming on the phone in his right hand, pushes the driver's door of his own parked car shut with his left hand, locks it with the key fob, and the indicator blinks once.

LOCATION MAP
Camera: a smartphone held in his right hand at chest height, about 70 centimetres from the car, pointing down and across at the driver's door. Foreground: the driver's door and its rain-beaded side window, the top of the wing mirror at the upper-left edge of frame. About 80° diagonal field of view, phone main-camera perspective, held at chest height about 70 centimetres from the door. Environment visible to the frame edges, deep edge-to-edge focus, no telephoto compression, no creamy bokeh.

CAMERA
Handheld in his own right hand at chest height while he stands still: slight hand sway, a small tilt corrected once by hand, no gimbal smoothness.

The car has real weight: suspension settles after it stops, tyres flex on the kerb, road grime along the sills, rain beads on the bonnet, reflections of the grey sky distort across the panels. Here it stands at the kerb under the street lamps, their reflections stretched across its wet panels.

Sound from the phone's microphone: close street sound, a little wind rumble, no voices.

> **MAKE TODAY.** Every generation in this video is **hands only** (EXTRA_MODE_C): no face, no Soul ID, no character sheet, no consent form. You can generate all five clips now. Only the **edit and the release** wait on you: G3 (whose profile it is), the credit decision (G2) and the owner's written OK to name the business and show its chart.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Category (your format)** | Client video 4: Before and after, 20–30 s |
| **Brand · website** | Coventry Airport Taxis 247 (its Google Business Profile) · coventryairporttaxis247.co.uk |

---

## What this video is

- **Concept.** Two plates filmed from exactly the same spot in a parked car, in exactly the same flat grey light. "May": the phone sits dark in its vent mount while the driver's fingers drum on the wheel. "August": the same frame, but the phone lights up twice and the hand lifts it out of the mount. The car never moves. Because the light, the rain and the framing are identical, the only difference the eye can find is **activity**.
- **Hook (0–2 s).** Split screen, May beside August, with the hook card `May: almost nothing. August: 32.` on screen from the first frame (the plan's wording; see the proposed change under "Exact on-screen wording").
- **Why this brand.** The Coventry Business Profile screenshot is the only real before-and-after inside one dated screenshot in the whole data set: almost nothing in May, the August marker sitting on the 32 gridline, 79 interactions in total. No archive or comparison export needed; we type only the printed 79 and the 32 gridline the August marker sits on.
- **What the edit reveals (14–22 s).** The real Business Profile chart rises between the two plates and is revealed month by month, in step with the plates. The May and August markers are ringed. The card says honestly that these are **interactions, not just calls**, that the line **peaked in August, then settled**, and that **October is a part month**.

**Deviations from the plan (one line each):**
- The phone sits in the **centre** vent at frame left, not "at frame right": from the passenger seat, only a centre-vent phone turned towards the driver keeps its screen edge-on to the lens (the same geometry as BR01_9x16).
- The **left** hand drums in May and lifts the phone in August (the plan says the right hand drums): the left hand is the one next to the centre vent, so the action and the phone share one crop for the split screen.
- The wiper **rests along the base of the windscreen** and returns there after its sweep, instead of "parked mid-glass": a single real wipe always parks at the bottom.
- The wiper sweep now has a visible cause: the driver flicks the stalk once (physics: cause before effect).
- A **CAMERA** block is added to the §8.3 worked prompt (it was folded into FORMAT MODE). The skeleton requires it.
- L-CAR-DAY drops "on that cheek", because no face is in frame (as §8.3 already does). The phone's glow is a second sentence after the unchanged light line.
- P-02's timeline gets a 2–3 s stage ("the light goes out") and a 7–8 s hold. The plan left 2–3 s and 7–8 s empty, and every range must be continuous.
- In the 9:16 hook the split is **top and bottom**, not left and right: a left/right split of a vertical frame leaves two 540 px strips, too thin to hold the hand and the phone together. The 16:9 keeps left and right.
- The 16:9 end beat uses `v04_B-01_9x16` in the series' "phone clip beside receipts" layout. The plan has no 16:9 B-01, and no extra generation is needed.
- When the owner's optional voice plays (22–25 s), the label switches to the §1.3 tier for a real voice over faceless footage: `Dramatised visuals. Real voice, real data.`
- The `32` gridline label inside the real screenshot is underlined, so viewers can see where the hook's "32" comes from. Nothing is redrawn.
- Memo distance is about 30 cm (production_rules A.3 and the character file), the same as every other file, not 20 cm.

## Script and voice memos

**The plates have no dialogue.** The driver never speaks. Any voice the model adds fails QC.

**Version A (preferred): one optional line from the real owner, voice only, over the last 3 s.** No generation of him at all. It needs his signed consent (voice only, box c) naming V04's case-study page and its 9:16 social posts, his written approval of the line, and his approval of both V04 cuts before release.

We send him **one question, never a sentence**:
> "Thinking back to this summer, what was August like for you?"

He answers in a relaxed memo of 1–2 minutes (`MEMO_CLIENT_COVENTRY_OWNER_v04_interview.m4a`). If he is already recording his V02 interview, add this question to the same session. We transcribe it and pick a line of **2 to 2.5 seconds**. He approves it in writing, then records it on its own.

| Time (both ratios) | Picture | Line | Who | Memo file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 22.0–24.6 s | `v04_B-01_9x16` (end beat) | `[APPROVED LINE 1 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT, about the summer, 2–2.5 s; for example "August was busy."]` | CLIENT_COVENTRY_OWNER, his real voice | `MEMO_CLIENT_COVENTRY_OWNER_v04_line1.m4a` |

**Rules for his line:** no numbers (the numbers are ours, on screen, with a source), no growth words ("kept climbing", "up", "doubled", "more and more"), no "No.1" or "first", no review wording, no "Ali". It must stay true after August, because the chart settles after August.

**How to record the memo (send this to him):**
- One line per memo. Three takes in the same file, with a 2-second gap between takes.
- A quiet room with soft furnishings (a lounge or a bedroom). No TV, radio, music or open window.
- Phone about **30 cm** from the mouth, slightly to one side so the breath doesn't pop.
- Voice Memos on its lossless setting, or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder, mono. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
- Say it the way you'd say it to a customer on the phone, not as if you were reading it.
- Send it full size by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. **Not WhatsApp.**
- File name: `MEMO_CLIENT_COVENTRY_OWNER_v04_line1.m4a`.

**Version B (fallback): no voice.** If there is no consent, or no approved line, the film runs on its native sound (rain, finger taps, the wiper, two phone buzzes) and the label stays `Dramatised reconstruction · Real data` throughout. Nothing else changes.

A single vertical frame of smartphone video, recorded on an overcast, drizzly afternoon inside a parked right-hand-drive family saloon on a wet Coventry kerb, engine off. The filming phone stands upright on a rolled-up jacket on the passenger seat, its lens at the driver's chest height and about one metre from the steering wheel, angled diagonally forward and across the cabin towards the driver's side. Right of it, the lower half of the steering wheel, its centre plain with no badge, and the driver seen only from the chest down: a plain dark everyday jacket with the cuffs pushed back a little at the wrists, plain dark trousers, the seatbelt off and hanging slack, both bare hands resting on the lower half of the rim, the left hand at eight o'clock close to the phone and the right hand at four o'clock; the top edge of the frame cuts across the driver's chest, and the shoulders and face are out of frame. The phone and the left hand both sit inside the middle half of the frame height. Upper part of the frame: the lower windscreen speckled with drizzle and short runnels, a faint band of condensation along its bottom edge, the wiper blades resting along its base; through it, soft and grey, the rear edge of the wet bonnet, a wet kerb with a puddle along the gutter, a grass verge, a concrete barrier and the rise of a ring-road slip road with a lamp post, any road sign turned away or out of frame. Right edge: the driver's door window with rain beads. Lower part: the gear lever, its plain knob with no markings, with a white charging cable looped over it, a half-empty plain water bottle with no label in the cup holder, and the edge of the grey passenger seat cushion in the bottom-left corner, soft. A parking ticket lies face-down and a little crooked on the dashboard by the windscreen; a film of dust on the dashboard top and a smudge on the inside of the glass. The instrument cluster and the dashboard screen are dark, with no clock showing. If car-interior photos are attached, take only the dashboard shape, materials and seat fabric from them and ignore any badges or text; if a hands photo is attached, take only hand shape, skin texture and proportions from it, not an identity. Flat overcast daylight through the windscreen is the only key, soft and slightly cool; the side window camera-right adds a brighter edge; the cabin roof and footwell fall into soft shadow; the windscreen itself is slightly overexposed. Real skin texture with visible pores and fine hairs on the backs of the hands; a plaster on one knuckle. Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each. About 80° field of view, deep focus from the gear lever to the slip road, no background blur. Muted colour inside a parked car as it really looks: a charcoal dashboard and grey seat fabric, rain beads on the glass, the world outside soft and grey; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated. No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable. Exactly one person visible, seen only from the chest down; no face and no reflection of a face anywhere, including the windscreen, the side glass and the dark back of the phone. Filmed handheld on a smartphone main camera: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.
```

- **Step 2 · Seedance 2.5 prompt:**

```
ASSET MAP
@Image 1: anchor still for this shot: framing, light direction, car-interior layout, the phone in its mount and the driver's hands in frame one; frame one matches this exactly; do not copy any text.

SCENE CONTEXT
On an overcast, drizzly afternoon a private-hire driver sits in a parked car on a wet Coventry kerb, engine off, waiting for work. His phone stays dark in its vent mount while the fingers of his left hand drum on the wheel, and he clears the windscreen with one sweep of the wiper.

LOCATION MAP
Camera: a phone standing upright on a rolled-up jacket on the passenger seat, lens at the driver's chest height, 1 metre from the steering wheel, angled diagonally forward and across the cabin towards the driver's side. Foreground: the soft edge of the grey passenger seat cushion in the bottom-left corner. Midground: at frame left, 60 centimetres from the lens, a plain black spring-grip mount on the centre air vent holding a phone in a plain dark case, turned to face the driver so only its side edge and the back of the case face the lens; right of it, the lower half of the steering wheel with the driver's hands on the rim; below, the gear lever, its plain knob with no markings, with a white charging cable looped over it and a half-empty plain water bottle with no label in the cup holder. Background: the lower windscreen with drizzle, a faint band of condensation along its bottom edge and the wiper blades resting along its base; beyond it, soft and grey, the edge of the wet bonnet, a wet kerb with a puddle along the gutter, a concrete barrier and the rise of a ring-road slip road with a lamp post. Right edge: the driver's door window with rain beads. A parking ticket lies face-down and a little crooked on the dashboard by the windscreen.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains the driver's hands on the wheel and the dark phone in its mount; no empty establishing frame.
The driver is seen only from the chest down, sitting in the driver's seat of the parked car: a plain dark everyday jacket with the cuffs pushed back a little at the wrists, both bare hands resting on the lower half of the steering wheel, five fingers on each hand, knuckle creases and veins visible. His face stays above the top edge of the frame and never enters it. The seatbelt is off and hangs slack; the jacket creases where the forearms rest, and the seat fabric dips under his weight.
The left hand rests on the rim at eight o'clock, within 30 centimetres of the phone; the right hand rests at four o'clock. The phone is dark, its screen turned towards the driver.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE. Camera static.

OPTICS
About 80° diagonal field of view, phone main-camera perspective, propped at chest height 1 metre from the wheel. Environment visible to the frame edges, deep edge-to-edge focus, no telephoto compression, no creamy bokeh.

CAMERA
The filming phone is propped on the seat and never touched; the frame stays static for the whole clip.
Focus and exposure stay steady on the wheel; the windscreen stays slightly overexposed throughout.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. Both hands rest on the wheel; the phone is dark. End state: still.
1-4s: The fingers of the left hand drum slowly on the rim, index finger to little finger, stop for a beat, then drum again; the right hand stays still. End state: the left fingers resting on the rim.
4-5s: At second 4 the left hand slips behind the rim and flicks the wiper stalk down once; the wiper starts to lift off the base of the glass. End state: the wiper halfway up the windscreen, the fingers leaving the stalk.
5-6s: The wiper finishes its single sweep, drags the drizzle into a smeared arc and drops back to rest along the base of the windscreen; the left hand returns to the rim. End state: left hand back on the rim, the wiper at rest, the glass cleared.

**No new generations.** The plan's fallbacks for V04 reuse Version A's clips or real captures:

| Fallback | When | What to make | Generations |

The edit uses exactly the five Version A clips: `v04_P-01_9x16`, `v04_P-02_9x16`, `v04_P-01_16x9`, `v04_P-02_16x9`, `v04_B-01_9x16` (prompts above). The label stays `Dramatised reconstruction · Real data` from start to finish | 0 |
| **Real-footage plates** (from `pack/characters/presenter-extras.md` §1) | A generated plate fails QC twice | Film the same shots for real on your phone (shot card below). They replace the failed clip one for one, except the May and August twins: if either plate of a ratio fails, film both plates of that ratio in one session without touching the camera phone, so they still start on the same frame | 0 |
| **Add-on 4b: York Cars old site → new site** | Only once York Cars confirms in writing who rebuilt the site and when **and** you send real Wayback or client captures | A separate short of about 12 s, built only from real captures (below). If the rebuild was Xoom Media's and not Hulk's, 4b is **not made** | 0 |

### Real-footage fallback: film the plates yourself (about 20 minutes)

A consenting colleague's real hands beat generated hands, every time. The film is still a staged reconstruction, so the label does not change.

- **The car:** any ordinary car, parked legally at a kerb (never on a taxi or station rank), **engine off**, on an overcast day. Drizzle helps. Tape over the badge on the steering wheel. Dashboard screen off. Park so no number plate is visible through the windscreen, or keep it soft and far away.
- **The camera phone:** rear main camera at 1x, Portrait mode and filters off. Stand it **upright** (9:16) on a rolled-up jacket on the passenger seat at the driver's chest height, about 1 m from the wheel, angled across to the wheel. Tap and hold on the wheel to lock focus and exposure. **Do not touch it between the May and August takes.** For the 16:9 pair, lay it on its side on the jacket, raised on a book so the lens stays at the driver's chest height.
- **The prop phone:** in a plain dark case, in a centre-vent mount, turned to face the driver. Set it to **vibrate only**, with notification previews off. Its screen must never face the camera.
- **The driver:** a plain dark jacket with the cuffs pushed back, no rings or watch, a plaster on one knuckle; head always out of frame. They sign the short hands-only OK first (`presenter-extras.md` §2) and are never named or captioned.
- **Takes (10 s each, same spot):** "May": hands on the wheel, the left hand drums, one flick of the wiper stalk, phone dark. "August": someone rings the prop phone, hangs up after one buzz, rings again; on the second buzz the left hand lifts the phone out of the mount and up out of frame. Nobody speaks. End beat: hold the camera phone at dashboard height about 40 cm from the prop phone lying face-down, ring it, the hand turns it face-up, screen edge-on to the lens.
- **Save as:** `grp_v04_P-01RF_t1_9x16.mp4`, `grp_v04_P-02RF_t1_9x16.mp4`, `grp_v04_P-01RF_t1_16x9.mp4`, `grp_v04_P-02RF_t1_16x9.mp4`, `grp_v04_B-01RF_t1_9x16.mp4`.

### Add-on 4b · York Cars: old homepage → live homepage (real captures only, no generation)

**Two conditions, both required:**
1. **York Cars confirms in writing** who rebuilt the site and in which month (our only date, about Nov–Dec 2025, is inferred from upload paths and unverified; the live footer says "Designed by Xoom Media"; Hulk's portfolio lists York Cars) and agrees we may show both versions. No confirmation, no 4b.
2. **Real "before" captures.** Our sandbox could not reach the Internet Archive (`research/wayback_before.md`: every request was reset or rate-limited). The captures have to come from your own browser, or from York Cars' or Hulk's own project records. **We never mock up an old site.**

It is a **separate short**, not part of the Coventry film: two different businesses in one 25 s film would blur whose data is whose.

**What to capture in your own browser (about 10 minutes, Chrome on a laptop):**
1. Open `https://web.archive.org/web/20250916232610/https://yorkcars.co.uk/`. Check that the date in the Wayback banner reads **16 September 2025**. If the address bar jumps to a different timestamp, write the new one down and use it in every file name below.
2. Check the page looks complete (styles and images loaded, not a plain list of links). If it is broken, open the calendar at `https://web.archive.org/web/2025*/yorkcars.co.uk`, pick the nearest complete capture **before November 2025**, and tell us which one you used.
3. **Provenance shot first:** with the Wayback banner and the address bar visible, take an ordinary screenshot of the whole browser window. Save it as `before_20250916232610_provenance.png`.
4. Switch to the toolbar-free address (add `if_` after the timestamp): `https://web.archive.org/web/20250916232610if_/https://yorkcars.co.uk/`. Close any cookie banner on the old page. **Do not edit, crop or retouch anything.**
5. **Desktop:** open DevTools (F12) → device toolbar (Ctrl+Shift+M / Cmd+Shift+M) → Responsive → **1440 × 900**. Press Ctrl+Shift+P (Cmd+Shift+P), type `screenshot`, choose **Capture screenshot** → `before_20250916232610_desktop.png`, then **Capture full size screenshot** → `before_20250916232610_desktop_full.png`.
6. **Mobile:** set the device toolbar to **390 × 844** with device pixel ratio **2**, reload, wait for the images, then **Capture screenshot** → `before_20250916232610_mobile.png` and **Capture full size screenshot** → `before_20250916232610_mobile_full.png`. These must match our "after" (`assets/sites/yorkcars/now_mobile_full.png` is 390 px at 2×, 780 px wide).
7. Send the five PNGs full size (Google Drive or email, **not WhatsApp**), or just send the timestamp and we run our capture script (`shot.js`) from a connection that can reach the archive.

**Optional, for the Coventry case-study page (not used in the V04 film):** the same steps for `coventryairporttaxis247.co.uk` at the **last complete capture before October 2024** and the **last before June 2026** (calendar: `https://web.archive.org/web/2024*/coventryairporttaxis247.co.uk`). Name them `before_<timestamp>_desktop.png` and so on. Even with them, there is no "we built" line until the SMEK footer question (G2) is settled, and the live site is shown only after the G11 fixes.

**The 4b edit (9:16, about 12 s, Hulk Marketing social):**

| Time | Picture | On screen |
|---|---|---|
| 0.0–0.8 | `before_…_mobile.png` inside a plain phone outline on the navy card | Chip from frame 1: `yorkcars.co.uk · Wayback Machine capture · 16 Sep 2025` |
| 0.8–4.0 | A slow real scroll down `before_…_mobile_full.png` | Same chip |

| 10.0–12.0 | End card | `Website rebuilt [month year] by [builder]`, both as confirmed in writing by York Cars, + brand lockup |

No performance claim (we have no York Cars data), no "No.1", no reviewer names, no generated footage, so no AI label; the source chips stay on throughout. A real scroll only: nothing on either page is redrawn.

### Sound, captions, labels, loudness, finishing

- **Sound:** Seedance's native rain, taps, wiper and buzzes are the soundtrack, crossfaded by 4 frames at every cut so the rain never jumps. Soft ticks on the underline and the two rings. **No music by default.** If you want a bed on the 9:16 only, one sparse licensed track at least 20 LU under the native sound, out by 22.0 and never under his line. No trending or copyrighted audio.
- **His voice (Version A):** his real memo laid in as recorded, lightly cleaned, no pitch or timing changes. Never a voice he hasn't heard and approved.
- **Captions:** only his line (Version A), word-timed, white with a soft shadow, Inter, two lines at most. 9:16: a band at 62–70% height. 16:9: bottom centre of the right two thirds.
- **Disclosure:** the label sits lower-left and small throughout (9:16 at about 76–79% height; 16:9 with a 40 px margin). Set the platform toggles on every post: TikTok AIGC, YouTube altered or synthetic content, Meta AI info. You and your adviser sign off the wording.
- **9:16 safe zones:** all text between 12% and 80% of the height (y 230–1536 of 1920), with 60 px side margins. Footage may run into the margins; text never does.
- **Loudness:** 9:16 at −14 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP. 16:9 web master at −16 LUFS (our default; tell us if your site player wants −14).
- **Finishing:** one grain value matched to the phone's sensor noise, one sharpen value, and **one identical light grade on all five clips** (lift the shadows a touch; never teal-and-orange), so May and August stay identical. Upscale once with Higgsfield `upscale_video` (ugc preset) only if you had to generate at 720p.
- **End card colours:** the case study uses GRP orange `#F7931E` / blue `#3FA9F5` on `#0B1628`, Inter. If the 9:16 goes out as Hulk Marketing, the rings, underlines and lockup switch to Hulk lime `#C6FA61` on `#121C17`.
- **Never on screen:** "calls" as the measure (it is interactions); any month value other than 32 and the total 79; "No.1", "#1", "first", "now", "just hit", "growth", "+%", up-arrows or count-ups; the Slough review widget or "4.9 / 202", "15,000+", "4.6", "100+ reviews"; the site's stock fleet or headset-operator images; "Qoute"/"Relaible" pages; any "Ali" review; clocks or time stamps; any "we built" line.

## What this video is

- **Concept.** On a wet Saturday night the York Cars manager walks us from the yard, through the office door, into the dispatch room, where York's night runs through one room. It is built only from York Cars' own photos of their yard and office. **Without those photos there is no V05.**
- **Hook.** A car door thunks in the wet yard on frame 1. The manager is already striding away from it, glances back at the phone filming them, and starts talking at second 1.
- **Why this brand.** York Cars is a 24/7 private-hire firm whose website is built for local search: a page for each of 15 suburbs and villages and 13 airports, and 2,695 Google reviews shown on the site. A night-shift tour shows the real business behind those pages.
- **What the edit reveals.** At 20 s (67%) the real review count from their own site lands as a receipt over the dispatcher's hands. At 24 s, over real York night footage, a capture of the site's navigation shows the location and airport pages. Both carry the caption `Context, not an agency result.` This is context about the client. It is **not** a result we claim.

**Changes from the plan (one line each):**
- Shooting order puts `v05_B-01` first: it has no identity and tests whether the dispatch room reads as real before the manager is generated (master_plan §7).
- `v05_W-01`: the manager has just parked and shuts the **driver's** door at second 0. The car points away from camera with its rear behind the camera, so neither plate can face the lens.
- `v05_W-01`: the operator walks 1.5 m behind and 0.5 m to the manager's **right**, and the manager glances back over the right shoulder. This is the plan's "a step behind and to the side", fixed to one side.
- `v05_W-01`, `v05_B-02`, `v05_P-01`: §2.2's L-STREET-NIGHT line is pasted verbatim (in P-01 without its face clause, see below), followed by one sentence placing the yard's real lamps. Set it from their night photos ("Set once" below).
- `v05_W-02`, `v05_B-01`, `v05_P-02`: the plan's SCREEN-SOFT is replaced by "every monitor angled away". A phone's deep focus can't blur a monitor 4 m away, and dispatch screens show customer addresses.
- `v05_B-02`: the plan's "three-quarter rear" view would show the rear plate. The camera now stands level with the rear bumper, looking forward along the car, so both plates stay out of frame.
- `v05_B-02` is made **only if York Cars confirms it fits child seats**. Otherwise the shot implies a service we haven't verified. The edit works without it.
- Edit: W-01 runs 0–12 s and W-02 runs 12–20 s, so line 2 finishes before the first receipt at 20 s. The plan had W-02 at 14–20 s, which would have cut line 2 short.
- Receipt R1 crops only the line "Based on 2,695 reviews", leaving out the stars, the Google logo and the reviewers' cards (no star average, no reviewer names, no Google marks).
- Fallback IDs `v05_P-01` and `v05_P-02` are new. The plan names the POV walk-round but gives it no IDs.
- Voice memos: the phone sits **30 cm** from the mouth (production_rules A.3), not 20 cm.
- `v05_P-01`: L-STREET-NIGHT's face clause is replaced (`each lamp lights its own pool of wet tarmac and the yard falls dark between them.`) because nobody is in frame.
- Night film: PAL-EXT and PAL-INT stay word for word, each followed by one night sentence (`Tonight the low cloud is dark, faintly lit by the town.` / `At this hour the window is black, with the room's tubes reflected in the wet glass.`). The VEHICLE lock is followed by `Here it stands on the yard's wet tarmac, the lamps' reflections stretched across its panels.` The plan's lines carry day words (white sky, daylight at the window, kerb).

## Script and voice memos

**DRAFT FOR CLIENT APPROVAL. Questions only.** We do not write the manager's sentences. They answer in their own words, we transcribe, they approve, and only then do the exact words go into Seedance. Until then the prompts carry `[APPROVED LINE 1 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT]` and `[APPROVED LINE 2 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT]`.

**Step 1: the interview memo.** Send them the two questions. They answer both in one relaxed memo, 1–3 minutes, as long as they like: `MEMO_CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER_v05_interview.m4a`.
1. "What does a Saturday night look like here?" → line 1
2. "What do customers ask for most?" → line 2

**Step 2: we pick one line per question** (5–6 s spoken, never more than 6 s, so it ends by second 7 of its clip), and they approve both in writing.

**Step 3: they record each approved line as its own memo.**

| Shot | Line | Starts at (in the clip) | Must end by | Memo file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v05_W-01` (both ratios) | [APPROVED LINE 1 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT] | second 1 | second 7 | `MEMO_CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER_v05_line1.m4a` |
| `v05_W-02` (both ratios) | [APPROVED LINE 2 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT] | second 1 | second 7 | `MEMO_CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER_v05_line2.m4a` |
| `v05_P-01`, `v05_P-02` (fallback) | The same two memos, laid in by us in the edit, unaltered | edit 1.0 s and 13.0 s | n/a | the same files |

**Rules for their lines:**
- **No numbers at all.** The numbers (2,695 reviews, 15 suburb and village pages, 13 airport pages) are ours, on screen, with their source.
- No "largest fleet", "number one", "best in York", "most trusted" or "Happy Users". No customer, driver or reviewer names, and no review quotes.
- No line about the agency ("Hulk got us…"): G2 is unresolved, and the film is context, not an agency result.
- If they mention a service (airport runs, students, the station), it must be one the site already lists.

**How to record a memo (send this to them):**
- One approved line per memo: three takes in the same file with a 2-second gap. Each take 5–6 s.
- Record in a quiet room with soft furnishings (a lounge or bedroom). Not the dispatch room with the radios on, and not the yard.
- Hold the phone about **30 cm** from the mouth, slightly to one side so the breath doesn't pop.
- Use Voice Memos on its lossless setting, or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder, in mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. Re-record any take that distorts.
- Say it the way you'd tell a new driver on their first night, not as if reading it out.
- Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. **Not WhatsApp.**
- Their accent is never described anywhere in a prompt. The memo carries the voice.

**Which memo goes where:** the best take is `@Audio 1` in W-01 (line 1) and W-02 (line 2). In the edit we lay their real memo in as the final voice wherever sync allows, with a light phone-at-1.5-metres EQ and the yard or room ambience under it. **If the generated voice doesn't sound like them, it fails QC** (production_rules G.1). Never ship a voice they haven't heard and approved.

**Final 30 s timing (both ratios; handles trimmed):**

| Edit time | Picture | Sound |
|---|---|---|
| 0.0–12.0 s | `v05_W-01` (clip 0.0–12.0 s): door thunk, the walk, the door pulled open | Door thunk at 0.0 s; line 1 at about 1.0–7.0 s; footsteps, puddle, door closer |
| 12.0–20.0 s | `v05_W-02` (clip 0.5–8.5 s), cut on the doorway | Line 2 at about 12.5–18.5 s; room tone, radio crackle with no words |
| 20.0–24.0 s | `v05_B-01` (clip 1.0–5.0 s): the dispatcher's hands | Typing, the handset lifted, radio crackle |
| 24.0–30.0 s | RF04, real York night footage (end card from 28.0 s) | Real street sound from RF04, ducked |

Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated. At this hour the window is black, with the room's tubes reflected in the wet glass. No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable. Every monitor is angled away from the camera; only its plastic back and stand are visible, and it gives off almost no light. Exactly one person visible: the dispatcher, seen only from behind. Filmed handheld on a smartphone main camera: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.

- **Step 2 · Seedance 2.5 prompt:**

```
ASSET MAP
@Image 1: anchor still for this shot: framing, light direction, the dispatcher's position and the room layout in frame one; frame one matches this; do not copy any screen content or text.
@Image 2: geography and materials of the firm's own dispatch office only (walls, desk, fittings, window); do not copy its camera angle; ignore any screens, signs, papers or printed text in it.
@Image 3: the dispatch desk with its radios and chargers only; do not copy its camera angle; ignore any screens or printed text in it.
@Image 4: the left hand of the person filming: hand shape, skin and proportions only; ignore its grey background and flat sheet light; it appears only on the desk from second 9.

SCENE CONTEXT
Late on a wet Saturday night, just in from the yard, the manager of a York private-hire firm walks into the small dispatch office filming the way ahead on the phone in their right hand, crosses to the desk where the radios charge and stops there while the dispatcher works at the back. It starts with the door closing behind the camera, crosses the room, and ends at the desk with a burst of radio crackle.

LOCATION MAP
Camera: the phone held upright in the right hand of the person who has just come in, at chest height, starting just inside the door at the left end of the front wall and facing into the room. The room is about 5 metres wide and 4 metres deep. Lower third of the frame: a worn grey floor with a grey cable taped across it. Middle: an empty swivel chair with a dark coat over its back, 2 metres in. Upper half, along the back wall 4 metres away: the dispatch desk with a row of handheld radios upright in their chargers at each end of the desk, two monitors on stands turned to face the right-hand end of the desk with only their backs seen, and the dispatcher right of centre with their back to the camera. Left edge of frame: a plain board of hooks with car keys on plain fobs and the corner of a counter with a kettle that has just boiled. A dark window with rain on the glass and a crooked blind is on the right wall, just out of frame.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already shows the room from just inside the door with the dispatcher in position; no empty or black opening frame. Nobody stands between the camera and the desk.
At the back of the room, one dispatcher sits at a desk with their back to the camera, small in frame and softly out of focus: plain dark everyday clothes, no logos or printed text, a radio headset over one ear, a lanyard turned round so only the plain back of the card shows. They lean a little towards a monitor that faces away; a radio handset stands on its charger within reach. Their face is never seen.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
About 80° diagonal field of view, phone main-camera perspective, held at chest height, pointing ahead into the room. Environment visible to the frame edges, deep edge-to-edge focus, no telephoto compression, no creamy bokeh.

CAMERA
Handheld by a person walking slowly: gentle vertical bob with each step, small horizon tilts corrected by hand, no gimbal smoothness.
The phone stays at chest height in the walker's right hand and points where they are going, then tilts down a little at the desk.
In the first second the auto white balance shifts slightly from the yard's cooler light to the green tint of the tubes, then settles.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. Behind the camera the office door swings shut on its closer and its latch clicks. End state: the camera still, just inside the door, looking into the room.
1-7s: The walker crosses the room slowly towards the left end of the desk, passing the empty chair with the coat on the right; steam from the kettle drifts up at the left edge of frame. End state: about half a metre from the desk edge, the radios close at the lower left of frame.
7-12s: The camera stops at the desk and tilts down a little; at second 9 the left hand of the person filming enters from the lower left of frame and rests flat on the desk edge beside the radio chargers, fingers spread, taking a little weight; at second 10 the dispatcher shifts in the chair and it creaks. End state: the hand flat on the desk at the lower left, the radios beside it, the dispatcher at the back.
12-14s: At second 12 a short burst of radio crackle with no intelligible words comes from the desk; the dispatcher reaches for a handset on its charger. Ambience only. End state: unchanged, the dispatcher's hand on the handset.

PHYSICS
Each step lands with weight on the hard floor and the frame bobs with it; steam from the kettle drifts up and thins in the tube light; the radios in their chargers rattle very slightly when the desk is touched; the office chair rocks back a little under the dispatcher and settles; the coat on the empty chair hangs still.

LIGHTING
Fluorescent ceiling tubes are the key, flat-ish but real with a slight green-cyan cast; the dark window adds nothing; darker corners at the back of the room; the monitors face away and give off almost no light. The tubes run across the middle of the ceiling, so the room is brightest in the middle and the floor, the corners and the space under the desk fall into soft shadow.
Real skin texture with visible pores and fine hairs on the backs of the hands; a faint ink mark on the side of one finger.
Plain dark everyday clothes; no logos, no printed text. Each incidental person is only partly in frame, seen from behind or from the chest down, and their face is never seen.
Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched; hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.

AUDIO
Ambience: a small dispatch office at night: a fluorescent tube buzzing faintly, a radiator ticking, rain against the dark window, a kettle settling after it has boiled, a radio hissing low on the desk.
Foley: the door closer's hiss and the latch click at 0 seconds behind the camera; the walker's own footsteps on the hard floor, close, from 1 to 7 seconds; keys chinking in a pocket; a soft press on the laminate at 9 seconds; the office chair creak at 10 seconds; a short burst of radio crackle at 12 seconds with a distant voice too broken to make out any words.
No dialogue. The incidental people do not speak. Any voices are distant and unintelligible, with no words that can be made out.
Sound from the phone's microphone: room tone, close footsteps, a little reflection off the hard walls.
No background music. No subtitles.

FINAL FRAME
The left end of the desk, with its radios, close at the lower left of the vertical frame, the dispatcher above and to the right reaching for a handset, the camera holding.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated. At this hour the window is black, with the room's tubes reflected in the wet glass.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
Every monitor is angled away from the camera; only its plastic back and stand are visible, and it gives off almost no light. The key fobs, the radios and the walls are plain, with no tags, rota boards or names.
Exactly one person visible in front of the camera: the dispatcher, seen only from behind. No extra people.
The only part of the person filming that is ever seen is their left hand on the desk from second 9.
Filmed handheld on a smartphone main camera: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.

## What this video is

- **Concept.** One plain question on screen, "What was it actually like working with Hulk?", answered by Organic Fostering's director or registered manager at the table in their own office at Beaumont House on Chester Road. A mug of tea they actually drink. A bus passes soft in the wet window behind them. Adults only.
- **Hook.** A plain question card (never a fake comment bubble) over real footage of Chester Road in drizzle with a bus passing (RF06, never a tram).
- **Why this brand.** It is the set's one regulated, non-taxi client, and the evidence is structural and true: a postcode check on the site and a library of plain-English guides. No performance data exists, so the film makes **no traffic, ranking or enquiry claim** and shows **no allowance figure at all**.
- **What the edit reveals.** After the answer, real dated captures of the live site: the postcode check (`/areas-we-cover`) and the guides index (`/blog`), then the card `61 pages · 32 plain-English guides`, sourced to the sitemap, with the context line `Site structure, not traffic results.` Then their last line, a half-smile and a sip of tea.

**Deviations from the plan (one line each):**
- Lengths are 30 s (16:9) and 29.5 s (9:16), not 25 s: their last line plus an unhurried sip needs 8.5 s, and each receipt needs about 2 s to be readable. Still inside your 20–30 s format.
- The first receipt lands at 15.5 s (52%), not 64%: it has to follow the answer, not cut into line 2.
- The site inserts come from new dated captures of `/areas-we-cover` and `/blog` (taken 22 Oct 2026), not from the homepage captures: the homepage shows live allowance figures (£20,837.44, £400.72) and photos of children.
- The sitemap source line reads "read 22 Oct 2026", not "lastmod 13 Sep 2026": the sitemap now has lastmod dates up to 22 Oct 2026 (the counts are unchanged: 61 URLs, 32 guides).
- In B-01 the pen draws a tick and a short line, not handwriting: generated handwriting turns into gibberish text.
- The window sits camera-left and wraps behind their right shoulder, so the bus is still "behind" them and the L-OFFICE light line stays verbatim.
- "Old Trafford" is kept out of every prompt: the words pull a football stadium into the window.
- New fallback IDs: `v06_B-01_9x16` (the 9:16 fallback needs a vertical hands shot) and `v06_B-01C_16x9` / `_9x16` (anonymous hands if the director gives no consent at all; the `C` on the shot marks an anonymous Mode C twin, the pack-wide hand-back convention used in V02, V09, V11 and V12). The plan names the hands shot but gives no vertical or anonymous version.
- The two vertical hands shots (`v06_B-01_9x16`, `v06_B-01C_9x16`) are filmed from behind the left shoulder, so the window is camera-right and their light line is the mirrored L-OFFICE line (window camera-right, left side darker). The face shots keep L-OFFICE as written; every hands shot (`B-01`, `B-01C`, both ratios) re-aims its face clause to "the hands and the notebook", because no face is in frame (as V08, V10 and V13 do).
- Memos are recorded with the phone about 30 cm away (production_rules A.3), not 20 cm, because 20 cm pops on breath.

## Script and voice memos

**DRAFT FOR CLIENT APPROVAL.** We send one question, never a sentence:

> "What was it actually like working with Hulk?"

**Step 1: the interview memo.** The director answers in their own words, as long as they like, in one file: `MEMO_CLIENT_OF_DIRECTOR_v06_interview.m4a`. We transcribe it and pick three lines. **They approve all three in writing** before recording them.

**What they may mention:** the plain-English guides, the postcode check, what the work was like day to day. **What they must not say:** any number, any allowance or income figure, "24/7", the Ofsted grade (unless the PDF has been checked), any traffic, ranking or enquiry result, any carer's or child's name or story, "No.1" or "first".

**Step 2: record the approved lines**, one file per line, three takes in each file with a 2-second gap.

| Memo file | Shot | Starts at (in the clip) | Longest it can be | On screen (16:9 / 9:16) | Line |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MEMO_CLIENT_OF_DIRECTOR_v06_line1.m4a` | `v06_A-01` (both ratios) | second 1 | **6 seconds** | 2.5–8.5 s / 2.0–8.0 s | [APPROVED LINE 1 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT] |
| `MEMO_CLIENT_OF_DIRECTOR_v06_line2.m4a` | `v06_A-01` (both ratios) | second 7 | **6 seconds** | 8.5–14.5 s / 8.0–14.0 s | [APPROVED LINE 2 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT] |
| `MEMO_CLIENT_OF_DIRECTOR_v06_line3.m4a` | `v06_A-02` (both ratios) | second 1 | **5 seconds** | 22.5–27.5 s / 21.5–26.5 s | [APPROVED LINE 3 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT] |

If a chosen line runs longer than its slot, we pick a shorter one from the transcript; we never speed it up.

**Version B instead:** they approve a **two-sentence written statement** (no recording needed). We show it as text: `[APPROVED STATEMENT SENTENCE 1]` / `[APPROVED STATEMENT SENTENCE 2]`.

**How to record a memo (send this to the director):**
- One approved line per file, three takes in the same file, 2 seconds of silence between takes.
- A quiet room with soft furnishings, door shut, **away from the main road** (not the office by the window).
- Phone about **30 cm** from the mouth, slightly to one side so breath doesn't pop.
- Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1/48 kHz recorder), mono, one voice, no TV, radio or music. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
- Say it the way you'd say it to someone thinking of fostering on the phone: calm, unhurried, not read out.
- Send full size by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. **Never WhatsApp.**
- Their accent is never described anywhere in a prompt. The memo carries the voice.

**If the generated voice in A-01 or A-02 doesn't sound like them, it fails QC.** We lay their real memo in as the final track wherever sync allows (production_rules G.1). Never ship a voice they haven't heard and approved.

It starts with a mug of tea held in both hands, turns as they set the mug down between lines, and ends with them sitting back after a bus has passed soft in the window behind.

LOCATION MAP
Camera on a tripod at seated eye height, about 2.5 metres from the director across the table, facing them and the window wall behind them. Foreground: the near corner of the table, out of focus, at the bottom left of frame. Midground: the director seated just right of centre; on the table a plain closed notebook with a plain pen on it, and a small potted plant with a few browning leaves. Background: a large window filling the left half of the frame and reaching behind the director's right shoulder, rain beads on the glass, a wet main road outside, soft and grey; a roller blind pulled a third of the way down, hanging slightly crooked; a radiator with chipped paint under the window. FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens character, camera 2 to 3 metres from the subject, natural human-eye perspective, zero obvious distortion, natural face proportions, background readable but softly out of focus.

CAMERA
Locked-off on a tripod with the faint micro-movement of a real head.
Focus stays on the eyes; one small natural focus correction when they lean forward to set the mug down.
The framing holds the director and the window together for the whole clip.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. They glance down at the mug, lift their eyes back to the interviewer and take a small breath in. End state: lips parted, about to speak.
1-7s: At second 1, @Image 1 the director says, in natural British English, "[APPROVED LINE 1 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT]", unhurried and warm, the mug held low at chest height, blinking naturally and glancing down once mid-sentence before looking back. On the last words they lean forward and set the mug down on the table by their right hand. End state: the mug on the table, right hand still loosely on its handle, eyes back on the interviewer.
7-13s: At second 7, @Image 1 the director says, in natural British English, "[APPROVED LINE 2 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT]", hands resting together on the table, one small open-palm gesture of the left hand on the key words, well below the chin. At second 9 a yellow city bus passes along the road outside, from the left edge of the window towards their right shoulder, a soft moving shape through the wet glass, gone by second 12. End state: the last word spoken, a small involuntary nod.
13-14s: They sit back a few centimetres in the chair and hold, breathing, eyes on the interviewer; ambience only.

PHYSICS
The mug has weight in their hands and pulls the wrists down slightly; when it touches the table the tea surface shivers and settles; the cardigan sleeves slide back a little on the forearms as they reach forward; the lanyard swings once and settles against the cardigan, the card still turned to the body; the chair takes their weight and creaks as they sit back; steam from the mug bends and thins in the window light; outside, the bus's tyres throw a faint spray off the wet road and rain beads on the glass stay put.

LIGHTING
Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-left is the only key; the right side of the face falls a stop darker with soft shadow under the cheekbone; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed.
Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched.

AUDIO
Ambience: a small office room tone, a radiator ticking, light rain on the window, occasional traffic on a wet main road muffled by the glass.
Foley: the mug set down on the table with a soft ceramic knock at 6 seconds; a bus engine and tyres hissing on the wet road outside from 9 to 12 seconds, muffled by the glass and kept low under the voice; a chair creak at 13 seconds.
Dialogue: only the quoted lines, spoken by the director at seconds 1 and 7, in natural British English; lips still when not speaking; no other voices.
Clean close dialogue as if from a clip-on microphone, natural room tone underneath, no echo.
No background music. No subtitles. At least 1 second of ambience-only before the first word and after the last word.

FINAL FRAME
The director sitting back a little, hands resting on the table, the mug by their right hand, eyes on the interviewer, the wet road empty again in the window behind; camera holding.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
The bus is a soft shape behind the wet glass with no readable destination, number or lettering and no people visible through its windows.

  - **Mug and hands:** the mug has weight, lands with a knock at 6 s and stays put; no hand ever near the mouth while talking. *Fail (floaty) → the physics block is in; next, one action per stage (drop the left-hand gesture).*
  - **Honesty:** no case files, children's pictures, whiteboards or certificates appear anywhere; no readable text. *Fail → remove the item from the location photo, remake the anchor still.*

Midground: an open plain notebook in the middle of the frame, both pages blank; the hands on it, entering from the lower edge, the cuffs of a plain dark navy jumper at both wrists. Top of frame, softly out of focus: the far edge of the table, a few browning leaves of a small potted plant at the top right, the bright edge of a window with a radiator under it along the right edge near the top. Window light from camera-right.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains both hands in position; no empty establishing frame. The right hand holds a plain pen, nib resting near the margin of the right-hand page, between a third and three fifths of the way down the frame; the left hand lies flat on the left-hand page, holding it open. No face in frame.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
29° diagonal field of view, short telephoto lens character, camera about 1.5 metres from the hands, the hands and the pen nib sharp, the mug in the foreground and the room behind softly out of focus, close framing through lens reach, not proximity.

CAMERA
Locked-off on a tripod with the faint micro-movement of a real head.
Focus stays on the pen nib and the right hand.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. The hands are still; the nib rests on the page. End state: nib touching the paper.
1-3s: The pen draws one small tick in the margin, lifts, then draws one short straight line beneath it. No letters, words or numbers are written. End state: a small tick and one short ink line on an otherwise blank page.
3-4s: The right hand lays the pen down across the open page and slides to rest at the notebook's edge. End state: pen lying on the page.
4-5s: The left hand leaves the page and curls around the mug's handle without lifting it; hold. End state: fingers on the mug handle, steam rising.

PHYSICS
The nib drags on the paper with slight friction and the page dimples under its pressure; the page corner lifts a few millimetres when the left hand leaves it, then settles; the pen rolls a few millimetres before it stops; the mug stays where it is when touched; steam bends and thins in the window light.

LIGHTING
Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-right is the only key; the left side of the hands and the notebook fall a stop darker with soft shadow; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed.
Real skin texture with visible pores and fine hairs on the backs of the hands; a faint ink mark on the side of one finger.
Plain dark everyday clothes; no logos, no printed text. Each incidental person is only partly in frame, seen from behind or from the chest down, and their face is never seen.
Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.

AUDIO
Ambience: a small office room tone, a radiator ticking, light rain on the window, occasional traffic on a wet road muffled by the glass.
Foley: the nib scratching on paper at 1 and 2 seconds; the pen laid down on the page at 3 seconds; a light tap of fingers on the mug at 4 seconds.
No dialogue and no voices. No background music. No subtitles.
Sound as recorded on the camera's microphone: close small sounds of movement, natural room tone, no echo.

FINAL FRAME
The pen lying across the open notebook beside a small tick and one short line, the left hand on the mug's handle, steam rising; camera holding.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
The notebook pages stay blank except for one small tick and one short line; no letters, words or numbers anywhere on the page.
Exactly one person, seen only as hands and jumper cuffs; no rings, no watch. No extra people.
Filmed on a handheld documentary video camera in available light: natural colour with a restrained grade, fine even digital grain, soft highlight roll-off on bright windows, real depth of field with a gently soft background.
```

- **QC (pass/fail):** the four checks of `v06_B-01C_16x9`, plus **vertical layout:** hands and nib between 35% and 60% of the frame height. *Fail → remake the still with the camera tilted further down.*
- **Save as:** `grp_v06_B-01C_t1_9x16.mp4`

## What this video is

- **Concept.** T1, the agency's SEO specialist, walks out of their real workplace in drizzle and tells their phone the most useful thing they learned this month. On the same taxi site, over the same three months, four ways of typing "Kenilworth taxi" sat at four different average positions: 6.7, 16.4, 8.6 and 8.5. Tiny wording differences behave like separate searches, so you check every variant.
- **Hook.** The real row 4 receipt (`kenilworth taxis · 6.7`) is on screen by 0.5 s, and row 13 (`kenilworth taxi · 16.4`) snaps in under it at 0.8 s. T1 is already mid-step on the front camera.
- **Why this brand.** Golden Line is the client with a verified Hulk footer credit and an attributed Search Console screenshot. These four rows are real, sit in one export, and need no comparison period. The lesson is true without any growth claim.
- **What the edit reveals.** As T1 says each number, we punch in on their face and the real Search Console row for that wording drops into the upper band. Four real receipts end up stacked, with the gap between 6.7 and 16.4 plain to see. A 1.4 s real Kenilworth clip (RF03) sits under "sixteen point four" and hides the join between the two takes.

**Changes from the plan (one line each):**
- **Re-grip moved** from second 6 to second 11 in `v07_A-01`. Second 6 is where line 2 starts, and a camera jolt during speech causes mouth mush (production_rules D.7).
- **VEHICLE lock added** to `v07_A-02`, where cars pass and stop in frame; §2.10 puts the lock in every prompt with a car exterior. `v07_A-01` has no car in frame, so it has no lock (a parked car added a plate risk and nothing to the story).
- **Bus shelter:** the plan's "unreadable advert" becomes a shelter **seen from its back, its advert panel turned away so only its plain grey metal back shows**. An advert face is the strongest text magnet on a street.
- **Crossing:** a signal-controlled crossing, because zebra crossings don't beep. Its push-button box (it carries a "WAIT" panel) is turned away from the lens.
- **Framing:** the head sits in the lower-middle of the frame so the four receipts fit the upper band inside the safe zone. The selfie line "top of the head nearly touching the top of the frame" is therefore not used.
- **Receipts:** a full Search Console row (1318 × 49 px) is unreadable at phone width. Each receipt therefore shows the row's **real query cell and real position cell side by side, with a visible gap**: two exact crops of the same row, nothing re-typed. The full-width rows appear on the post's cover frame. We use the §1.2 orange **underline**, not the plan's "ring", so V07 matches the series.
- **Light:** L-STREET is pasted verbatim, plus one sentence per shot naming which side of the face is brighter. A flat overcast line on its own invites the even, shadowless "render" look. In the hands-only fallback `P-01`, its "soft shadows under the eyes and chin" becomes "soft shadows under the hands and the phone", because no face is in frame (as V13's H-01 does).
- **No breath vapour.** It is a daytime shot at around 10 °C. The atmosphere is drizzle instead.
- **Fallback:** given the ID `v07_P-01_9x16` (the plan names the shot but gives no ID). The thumb types over the lower third of the green screen, which relaxes SCREEN-GREEN's "one brief tap", because typing is the action. The four corner dots stay clear, and we key around the thumb.
- **Memo distance:** about 30 cm, as in production_rules A.3 and T1's character file, so every memo in the set is recorded the same way.
- **A-02 ends on the turn, not the step off the kerb.** The last second held the beep, a glance back, the laugh, a full turn and a step, which breaks one-change-per-stage and smears the face in the second the end card uses. It now holds the beep, the laugh and the start of the turn. The cut ends at 20.0 s (clip 9.0–9.9 s).

## Script and voice memos

**Agency draft.** T1 edits it, approves it in writing and records it. Numbers are said as words and must match the receipts exactly. If T1 changes the wording, the numbers stay exactly as written. **If T1 changes any word, paste their approved wording into the quoted line in the A-01/A-02 TIMELINE before generating, and send it to us for the captions.**

| Shot | Starts at (in the clip) | Line (draft) | Length | Memo file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v07_A-01_9x16` | second 1 | "Thing I learned this month. Same taxi firm, same town, same three months." | about 4–5 s, ends by second 6 | `MEMO_T1_SEO_v07_line1.m4a` (+ `_outdoor`) |
| `v07_A-01_9x16` | second 6 | "Kenilworth taxis: six point seven. Kenilworth taxi, no S: sixteen point four." | about 5 s, ends by second 11 | `MEMO_T1_SEO_v07_line2.m4a` (+ `_outdoor`) |
| `v07_A-02_9x16` | second 1 | "Taxi Kenilworth: eight point six. Taxis Kenilworth: eight point five." | about 4 s, ends by second 5 | `MEMO_T1_SEO_v07_line3.m4a` (+ `_outdoor`) |
| `v07_A-02_9x16` | second 5 | "Four ways to say it. Four different searches. So I check every one." | about 4 s, ends by second 9 | `MEMO_T1_SEO_v07_line4.m4a` (+ `_outdoor`) |

**Rules for the lines:**
- The only numbers allowed are six point seven, sixteen point four, eight point six and eight point five, each with its own wording. They are **average positions over 19 Jul–18 Oct 2026**.
- No "now", "just hit", "moved", "climbed", "page one" claims, "number one", "top" or "first". No "we ranked them" or other causal lines.
- "Same town" means the town searched for (Kenilworth). The firm is Golden Line in Warwick, and the context strip says so. T1 must not name the firm aloud unless Golden Line agrees in writing.
- "Thing I learned this month" must be true for T1. If it was last month, T1 says so.

**How to record a memo (send this to T1):**
- Use a quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a lounge or bedroom (not a kitchen or stairwell). No TV, radio or music.
- Hold the phone about **30 cm** from your mouth, slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop (production_rules A.3).
- Use Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
- **One line per memo**: three takes per line, each saved as its own file (`MEMO_T1_SEO_v07_line<n>_t1.m4a`, `_t2`, `_t3`). Each take must fit its slot: lines 1 and 2 under 5 s, lines 3 and 4 under 4 s; if one runs long, say it a little quicker. We keep the best one as `MEMO_T1_SEO_v07_line<n>.m4a`.
- Say it the way you'd tell a colleague over a coffee, not as if reading.
- **Then record all four lines a second time outdoors** on the V07 pavement, phone at arm's length, walking slowly for lines 1–2 and standing at the crossing for lines 3–4. Save them as `MEMO_T1_SEO_v07_line<n>_outdoor.m4a`. We use them where they line up with the lips, and under RF03.
- Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. **Not WhatsApp.**
- T1's accent is never described in any prompt. The memo carries the voice.

**Which memo goes where:** the clean indoor take is the `@Audio` reference in Seedance, because it guides timbre and pace best. In the edit the final track is T1's real voice: the indoor take bound as `@Audio`, with a light phone-mic EQ under the clip's own ambience; an `_outdoor` take only where it lines up within two frames, or under RF03. **If the generated voice doesn't sound like T1, that is a QC fail** (production_rules G.1). Never publish a voice T1 hasn't heard and approved.

**Final 20 s timing (handles trimmed; full table in the edit plan):**

| 0.0–1.0 s | `v07_A-01` (clip 0.0–1.0 s): T1 mid-step | Street ambience, footsteps |

Midground: the SEO specialist, head and shoulders, standing on the blister paving at the kerb edge with their back three-quarters to the road. Background, mostly in focus: the wet road running across the frame from left to right about 2 metres behind their shoulders, a row of square metal studs marking the crossing; the far lane's stop line is just off the left edge of frame; across the road, the far pavement and building fronts, too small and far to read, every sign angled away or out of frame. At the left edge of frame, a grey signal pole with its push-button box turned away from camera and its signal head seen from the side.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains the SEO specialist in position; no empty establishing frame. They stand still at the kerb, head and shoulders in the lower-middle of the vertical frame, a little right of centre, the top of the head about 40 percent of the way down from the top edge of the frame, the road crossing the frame behind their shoulders. Their right upper arm runs out of the lower-left edge towards the phone. Torso faces the camera, turned slightly towards the road on camera-left; eyes on the screen just below the lens; lips closed. Their left hand hangs at their side below frame. A plain dark grey hatchback is passing side-on in the far lane behind them, from left to right.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
About 80° diagonal field of view, phone front-camera perspective, lens 40 to 55 cm from the face at arm's length, slightly above eye level. The face sits close and slightly enlarged at the centre, background visible to the frame edges and mostly in focus, straight lines stay straight, no portrait bokeh.

CAMERA
The phone is held in the speaker's own outstretched right hand; the frame moves with their arm: slight handheld micro-shake, small drifts as they gesture with the other hand, a natural re-grip once.
Auto exposure breathes slightly when the bright sky comes into frame, then settles.
Their eyes flick between the lens and the screen image of themselves, as people do on a front camera.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. They stand still; the grey hatchback finishes passing behind them and leaves the right edge of frame, its tyres hissing; they re-grip the phone once and the frame settles. End state: lips parted, about to speak.
1-5s: At second 1, @Image 1 the SEO specialist says, in natural British English, "Taxi Kenilworth: eight point six. Taxis Kenilworth: eight point five.", unhurried, with one small nod on each number. At second 3 a plain white van with no lettering passes side-on in the near lane behind them from right to left, its spray drifting in the drizzle. End state: line finished, lips closed, eyes on the lens.
5-9s: At second 5, @Image 1 the SEO specialist says, in natural British English, "Four ways to say it. Four different searches. So I check every one.", a little lighter in tone. On "four ways" their left hand rises into the lower edge of frame at chest height, palm open, and drops again, away from the mouth. At second 6 a dark saloon slows and stops side-on in the far lane at the stop line at the left edge of frame, its nose dipping as it brakes and settling back on its suspension. End state: line finished, lips closed, a half-smile, the road behind them still.
9-10s: At second 9 the crossing starts to beep; they give a small breath of a laugh through the nose with lips closed and start to turn their head and shoulders towards the road; the phone tilts with their arm and the bright sky edges into the top of frame. End state: head turned towards the road, a half-smile, the frame tilting.

PHYSICS
They stand with their weight on one leg and shift it once onto the other; the open jacket fronts hang still, then swing a little as they start to turn at second 9; drizzle beads darken the jacket shoulders; the passing vehicles' tyres throw thin spray that falls back onto the road; puddles in the gutter ripple after each tyre.
The car has real weight: suspension settles after it stops, tyres flex on the kerb, road grime along the sills, rain beads on the bonnet, reflections of the grey sky distort across the panels.

LIGHTING
Flat overcast sky as a huge soft source from above; soft shadows under the eyes and chin; wet tarmac reflects the grey sky; no direct sun. In this shot the open sky over the road behind them, a little to camera-left, lights the camera-left side of the face a touch brighter, and the other side falls a little darker.
Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched.

AUDIO
Ambience: a town-centre crossing at lunchtime in drizzle: tyres hissing on the wet road, drizzle ticking on metal, distant traffic, a door closing somewhere across the road.
Foley: the hatchback's tyre hiss fading out at second 1; the van's tyre hiss and engine passing at second 3; a soft brake squeak and an idling engine from second 6; the crossing's rapid electronic beeping from second 9; a jacket rustle at second 9.
Dialogue: only the quoted lines, spoken by the SEO specialist at seconds 1 and 5, in natural British English; lips still when not speaking; a small breath of a laugh through the nose at second 9, no words; no other voices.
Sound recorded by the phone's built-in microphone at arm's length: close voice with a little reflection off the building fronts, faint handling noise when the grip shifts, a little wind rumble.
No background music. No subtitles. At least 1 second of ambience-only before the first word and after the last word.

FINAL FRAME
The SEO specialist's head turned towards the road, a half-smile, the bright sky edging into the top of frame, the stopped car at the left edge, the frame tilting with their arm.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted autumn colour as it really looks: wet slate greys, an overcast white sky, wet black tarmac, red-brick terraces and cream stucco, cold white LED and older amber street light; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
Every vehicle is plain, with no livery or lettering, and passes or stops side-on, its number plates never facing the camera; each driver is never more than a dark shape behind the wet glass. The push-button box stays turned away from camera.
Exactly one person visible. No extra people.
Filmed handheld on a smartphone front camera at arm's length: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.

## What this video is

- **Concept.** T1 films their own laptop on their phone at the agency desk and talks through one honest idea: `coventry airport transfers` is **averaging position 6.0** over three months, and about **one in ten** times it's shown, someone clicks (10.5% CTR). Then the candid part: **small numbers**, 76 times shown, 8 clicks.
- **Hook (0–0.8 s).** The real Search Console row pops up full width before anything else: `coventry airport transfers · avg 6.0 · 10.5% CTR`, with T1's first words already playing.
- **Why this brand.** The row is real, page one on average, with the best click-through in Coventry's top five. It is also the honest answer to your original brief, "this keyword just hit position 3": **no row sits at 3, and there is no earlier period to compare.** So the film says "is averaging" and states it plainly.
- **What the edit reveals.** We key the real Search Console screenshot into the laptop's green screen and scroll it in time with the generated hand. Each number gets its own exact crop as it is spoken. The film closes on the rainy window and one line of context: these are three-month averages, so nothing has "just hit".

**Deviations from the plan (one line each):**
- **Label:** `Dramatised visuals. Real voice, real data.` (the §1.3 tier for a real voice over faceless footage) replaces the plan's non-standard `Illustrative footage. Real data. Real voice.`
- **Edit timeline:** P-01 is 14 s long, so it can't cover the plan's 1–20 s. It now runs 0.8–12.0 s. A full-frame receipt card carries the "small numbers" line (12–18 s), and P-03 moves to 18–24 s so its keyed row 3 sits under its own line ("Coventry airport taxi, averaging seven"). P-02 stays at 24–30 s.
- **P-02 turns up and to the LEFT**, not right. L-OFFICE puts the window camera-left, and P-01 puts the mug left of the laptop.
- **L-OFFICE** swaps "the right side of the face … under the cheekbone" for "the right side of the hand and the keyboard", because there is no face in frame. The rest is verbatim. In P-02 one sentence is added for the moment the window comes in front of the lens.
- **SCREEN-GREEN** is adapted in P-02 (only one corner is in frame, for 1–2 s) and in P-03 (a close frame shows only the lower half of the screen and its two lower dots). We track the visible dots plus the bezel edges.
- **P-02 gets a second still** (an end keyframe of the window and mug), so Seedance doesn't have to invent what the camera turns to.
- **Hook and receipt cards** use exact **sub-crops** of row 4 and the header (the query cell and the four number cells) at 1.85×. Nothing is redrawn. The full 1318 px row would be about 40 px tall on a phone and unreadable.
- **Audio lock:** "No voices, near or distant" replaces the extras' "distant, unintelligible voices", so nothing competes with T1's voice-over.
- **P-03's tap** is used in the edit as the moment row 3 is outlined on screen.
- Memo distance is about **30 cm** (production_rules A.3 and T1's character file), the same as every other file, not 20 cm.
