## Script and voice memos

**The clips have no dialogue.** Nobody in them speaks, and any voice the model adds fails QC. The whole voice-over is **T1's real voice**, recorded on their own phone and laid in by us. It is never generated and never cloned.

**Who records:** T1, the SEO specialist (identity still to be confirmed by you). If T1 says no, any consenting team member records the same lines; the voice tag then carries their own first name and real job title. Nothing else changes.

**The lines (agency draft; T1 edits and approves each one in writing first, and the approved wording is what we caption).** Numbers are written as words, and every one matches the receipt on screen.

| Slot in the cut | Line | Matches on screen | Memo file |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.0–6.0 s | "Coventry airport transfers. Averaging position six over the last three months." | Row 4: position **6.0**; dates 19 Jul–18 Oct 2026 | `MEMO_T1_SEO_v08_line1.m4a` |
| 6.0–12.0 s | "That's page one. And about one in ten times it's shown, someone clicks." | Row 4: CTR **10.5%**; context `Positions 1–10 are page one.` | `MEMO_T1_SEO_v08_line2.m4a` |
| 12.0–18.0 s | "Small numbers: seventy-six times shown. Eight clicks." | Row 4: **76** impressions, **8** clicks | `MEMO_T1_SEO_v08_line3.m4a` |
| 18.0–24.0 s | "Coventry airport taxi, averaging seven." | Row 3: position **7.0** | `MEMO_T1_SEO_v08_line4.m4a` |
| 24.0–30.0 s | "No just hit here. These are three-month averages." | Context strip | `MEMO_T1_SEO_v08_line5.m4a` |

**Rules for the lines:** impressions are always "times shown", never "people saw" or "people searched". Never say "number one", "first", "now", "up" or "growth", and never say "we built" or "our client". If T1 rewords a line, the numbers stay exactly as written. Each line must fit in **5.5 seconds** at a relaxed pace, which all five do.

**Delivery:** candid and unhurried, like showing a colleague something on your screen. The last line is plain and flat, not a punchline.

**How to record each memo (send this to T1):**
- **One line per memo.** Three takes in the same file, with a 2-second gap between them.
- Use a **quiet room with soft furnishings** (a lounge or a bedroom, or a meeting room with the door shut). Not the kitchen, a stairwell or the open office. No TV, radio, music or open window.
- Hold the phone about **30 cm from your mouth**, slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop.
- Use Voice Memos on its **lossless** setting (iPhone: Settings → Apps → Voice Memos → Audio Quality → Lossless), or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder, in mono. Speak at normal volume. If a take sounds distorted or clipped, record it again.
- Read the numbers exactly as written ("seventy-six", not "seven-six").
- Send the files **full size** by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. **Not WhatsApp.**
- File names: `MEMO_T1_SEO_v08_line1.m4a` to `MEMO_T1_SEO_v08_line5.m4a`. Tell us which take you prefer in each file.

**Version B1 lines (Golden Line data)** are in the fallback section. They are recorded **only** if B1 is triggered.

Foreground: at the lower-left frame edge, 25 centimetres from the lens and cut in half by the frame, an orange enamel mug with a small chip on the rim, a thin thread of steam rising from it; the near edge of the desk along the bottom of the frame. Midground: the open laptop in the middle of the frame, its screen a little above centre and filling about two thirds of the frame width; below it the keyboard deck and the trackpad; the right hand on the trackpad, entering from the bottom-right edge. A white charging cable runs from the laptop's left side across the desk and over its edge; a plain grey notebook lies face-down at the right edge, cut off by the frame. Window light from camera-left.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains the laptop with its green screen, all four corner dots visible, and the right hand on the trackpad; no empty establishing frame.
Only one person's bare hand is in frame, close, entering from the bottom-right edge, the forearm in a plain mid-blue overshirt sleeve with its cuff at the wrist, no logos or printed text, five fingers, knuckle creases and veins visible. The shoulders and face stay out of frame. The fingertips press and flatten slightly on whatever they touch, and the forearm takes its weight on the edge of the desk.
The index and middle fingers rest on the lower half of the trackpad; the thumb rests against the palm rest. The other hand is out of frame, holding the phone. The hand stays below the keyboard's top row and never touches or crosses the screen.

SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

Sound from the phone's microphone: close room tone, faint handling noise when the grip shifts.
No background music. No subtitles. At least 1 second of ambience-only at the head and the tail.

FINAL FRAME
The lower half of the flat green screen across the top fifth of the frame with both lower corner dots sharp, the keyboard and trackpad below, the hand at rest at the lower-right of the trackpad, the frame steady.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
One small warm orange object in frame, such as a mug or a notebook.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
The visible lower half of the laptop screen shows a flat, uniform, matte chroma-green fill from edge to edge, evenly lit, with no interface, no text, no reflections and no glare; its two lower corners and the bezel stay visible, with one small dark dot in each lower corner of the green. The screen gives off almost no light.
The keyboard's key legends are worn and too small to read; the laptop has no logo and no stickers.
Exactly one person visible, seen only as one hand and forearm; no face and no reflection of a face anywhere. No extra people.
Filmed handheld on a smartphone main camera: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.
```

- **QC (pass/fail):**
  - **Trackable screen.** Both lower dots and both side edges of the bezel are visible for all 8 s, the green is flat, and nothing shows on it. *Fail:* region edit to flat green. If a dot drifts out of frame, remake the still with the phone a little further back.
  - **Keys unreadable.** This is the highest-risk shot for gibberish letters on keycaps.
    - *Fail:* region edit (`EDIT TARGET: Edit @Video 1, seconds 0-8 only. CHANGE: the key legends become faint, worn and unreadable. PROTECT: the hand, the screen, the camera, the light and the sound.`). Otherwise we soften the keys in the edit.
  - **One tap, with weight.** The finger travels, hovers, then taps once at about 4 s with an audible click and a tiny lid shiver. There is no double tap and the finger never touches the screen.
    - *Fail (floaty or several taps):* replace the 1-3s line with `1-3s: The index finger moves slowly to the centre of the trackpad and stops just above it. End state: the fingertip over the centre of the pad.` and regenerate. Next, attach `REF_HANDS_C_05.jpg` to the still.
  - **Hand.** Five fingers, the chipped thumbnail, the mid-blue cuff, pores and fine hairs, no waxy sheen.
    - *Fail (plastic skin):* check the still was not glossy and remake it. Only then add `natural skin texture on the hands, visible pores and fine hairs, no smoothing.` after the skin line.
  - **Sound.** One click at 4 s, plus rain and room tone. No voice, no music.
- **Save as:** `grp_v08_P-03_t1_9x16.mp4`

### B2 · Real footage: film the three shots yourself (about 20 minutes)

A real hand on a real desk beats generated hands every time. The plan prefers this to generation.

- **Whose hand:** T1's own, or a consenting colleague's after the short hands-only OK (`presenter-extras.md` §2). Wear a plain mid-blue overshirt. No watch with a logo, no rings. A real plaster or chipped nail is fine.
- **The desk:** your real desk by a window, on a grey day. Use the orange enamel mug with hot tea, so it steams. Run the charging cable across the desk, and lay a notebook face-down. Turn every paper over, put tape over the laptop's logo and any stickers, and take nothing off the walls just for the shot (never dress the room up as a bigger office).
- **What's on the laptop screen.** Pick one option:
  - **Option 1 (recommended, simplest):** a flat green full screen. Open a new browser tab, type `data:text/html,<body style="margin:0;background:rgb(0,177,64)">` into the address bar, press Enter, then go full screen (F11 on Windows, Ctrl+Cmd+F on a Mac). Turn on Do Not Disturb first. In Chrome on a Mac, untick View → Always Show Toolbar in Full Screen. Set the screen brightness to about 40% so it doesn't light the hand green. We track the real corners of the bezel and key in the real screenshot, exactly as for the generated clips.
  - **Option 2 (fully in-camera):** open our receipt file `coventryairporttaxis247_gsc_3m_full.png` in the browser at 100% (we'll send it), go full screen, and scroll it for real. Start below the Search Console header, so your account picture never shows. **Do not film the live Search Console:** its numbers move day to day and must match `gsc_data.json` exactly.
- **The camera phone:** rear main camera at 1×, held upright (9:16) in your left hand, elbow on the desk. Portrait mode, filters and the flash off; video at 1080p, 25 or 30 fps. Don't lock focus: one natural focus hunt is welcome.
- **The takes:**
  - **P-01_RF (14 s):** from your seat, about 55 cm from the screen. Hand resting, two slow scrolls with a pause, then the hand settles on the palm rest.
  - **P-02_RF (6 s):** start on the laptop's lower-left corner, then swing slowly up and left to the rainy window and the mug, and hold.
  - **P-03_RF (8 s):** about 40 cm from the screen, angled down over the keyboard. One finger moves to the trackpad and taps once.
  - Nobody speaks. No music or radio in the room. Shoot three takes of each.

### Sound, captions, labels, loudness, finishing

- **Voice:** T1's real memos, the chosen takes laid in as recorded. Light noise reduction and a gentle high-pass only: no pitch or timing changes, no AI voice repair. Never publish a voice T1 hasn't heard and approved.
- **Native sound:** Seedance's room tone, rain, trackpad whispers, the click and the grip rubs stay. They sit about 15 dB under the voice, with 4-frame crossfades at every cut so the rain never jumps. Soft ticks on each underline move.
- **Music:** **none by default.** It's a candid talk-over-a-laptop clip, and music makes it read like an ad. If you want a bed, use one sparse licensed track at least 20 LU under the voice, out by 28.0. No trending or copyrighted audio.
- **Captions:** word-timed, white with a soft shadow, Inter, two lines at most, in the 62–70% band. Numbers appear as figures (6, 1 in 10, 76, 8, 7), with "just hit" in quotes.
- **Disclosure:** the label sits lower-left and small throughout. Set the platform toggles on every post: TikTok AIGC, YouTube altered or synthetic content, Meta AI info. You and your adviser sign off the wording.
- **9:16 safe zones:** all text between 12% and 80% of the height (y 230–1536 of 1920), with 60 px side margins. Footage may run into the margins; text never does.
- **Loudness:** −14 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP.
- **Screen key (master_plan §9):**
  - Tracking: corner-pin on the four dots (in P-02 and P-03, a planar track on the visible dots plus the bezel edges).
  - Insert brightness: set it to about 85% white with a slight cool cast, so it sits in a daylit room rather than glowing.
  - Surface: a soft glare pass from the window side (left), a 1–2 px chromatic edge, faint moiré and a grain match.
  - Spill: a faint cool-white spill from the page onto the keyboard deck, the trackpad and the top of the hand (P-01, P-03), so the bright page reads as lighting the desk.
  - Match the camera: copy P-01's focus hunt at src 5–6 s (the insert softens with it) and every punch-in, and match the motion blur on P-02's swing.
- **Finishing:**
  - One grain value matched to the phone's sensor noise, one sharpen value, and one light grade across all three clips (lift the shadows a touch; never teal-and-orange).
  - Upscale once with Higgsfield `upscale_video` (ugc preset), only if you had to generate at 720p.
- **Optional 16:9 reuse (Coventry case-study page, "phone clip beside receipts"):**
  - Layout: the 9:16 master in a rounded phone frame on the left third of a 1920 × 1080 navy card. R6 (the full row 4) builds on the right two thirds at 0.9×, then R4/R5, with the source line and context strip under them.
  - Mix the web master at −16 LUFS.
  - It only goes live once G11's Coventry site fixes are done, if the page also shows the live site.
- **Never on screen:** "No.1", "#1", "first", "now" as a claim, "growth", "+%", up-arrows or count-ups; "people saw" or "people searched"; "last quarter"; "15,900" (it's 15.9K, and not used here anyway); the Coventry site's Slough review widget, "15,000+" or "4.6"; any "Ali" review; clock or time stamps; any credit line before G2.

## What this video is

- **Concept.** On a wet afternoon between jobs, the owner of Leam Taxis is parked on a Leamington terraced street (at a kerb, never on a rank), engine off, reading the monthly report on his phone. A second phone propped in his dash mount films him. The reaction is small: he reads, scrolls back to check, breathes out a short laugh, maybe says one word to himself, rubs the back of his neck and looks out at the rain. It is labelled as a re-creation.
- **Hook.** A 1.5 s stitch of V03 (his "…twenty-five"), with the real September tooltip on screen by 0.8 s, then a hard cut into his car.
- **Why this brand.** Leam Taxis' Business Profile shows **25 calls in September 2026**, read exactly from the tooltip, the best of the six months shown. A September report is the one moment where that number lands, and V12 (T2 sending the report) and V03 (the owner's milestone) both lead into it.
- **What the edit reveals.** The real tooltip is keyed into the green screen of his phone, then pushed to full frame with its source line. The end card is the real headline-and-chart crop with its own range, `May–Oct 2026 (October part month)`. **Never** "best month since May", and never "114 calls since May" after a September report.
- **Best of all (plan):** he films the real moment himself next month, and we use that instead (Version B1 below).

**Changes from the plan (one line each):**
- The plan's table points to "worked prompt §9.2". The worked prompt is master_plan **§8.2**, which this file builds on.
- The disclosure label: the plan's edit line says `Re-creation made with [Name]'s permission. Real data.`, which drops "AI". We use the §1.3 wording: `AI re-creation made with [Name]'s permission. Their words, their voice. Real data.` It is true even if he stays silent in R-01, because the V03 stitch carries his own approved words and voice. With no V03 stitch and no word, it becomes `AI re-creation made with [Name]'s permission. Real data.`
- R-01 framing: §8.2 says both "head and shoulders in the lower two thirds" and "the top of the head close to the top edge". These conflict, and the phone held low has to stay in frame. So his head sits in the upper part of the frame, near the top edge, with his hands and phone along the bottom.
- R-01 final frame: §8.2 ends with "the phone lowered to his lap", but its timeline never lowers it. Lowering it as well as the neck rub and the turn would crowd one 3 s stage, so the phone stays low in his right hand at the bottom edge of frame to the end.
- R-01 dressing: the camera sits on the dash, so the dash is behind the lens. The face-down parking ticket stays on the dash in B-01, where it can be seen. In R-01 the uncomposed elements are the dangling charging cable and a face-down receipt on the passenger seat.
- R-01 light: the phone's glow slips off his face as he turns away at second 7. The screen-left side of his face falls a little darker, and a faint smudge on the front lens hazes the bright window (the windscreen key sits behind the camera). Otherwise L-CAR-DAY and GLOW are pasted verbatim.
- B-01 and H-01 light: no face is in frame, so L-CAR-DAY drops "on that cheek" (the §8.3 no-face wording).
- B-01: the PHONE-REAR optics block says 1–2 m. Here it is about 50 cm, because the shot is an insert of the phone.
- B-01: "one scroll at 2 s" is written as one short thumb swipe, after which the thumb goes back to the edge of the phone. That fits SCREEN-GREEN's "at most one brief touch".
- B-01: "held still" over the shoulder implies someone else is holding the phone. It is written as a phone steadied by someone leaning in from the back seat, who is never seen.
- B-01: the instrument panel behind the wheel is stated as dark (engine off), so no lit dials or numbers can be generated.
- New fallback ID `v09_H-01_9x16` (8 s): a 15 s hands-only cut needs a reaction beat, and B-01 alone is 5 s. It is not in the 86-take count.
- R-01's anchor still uses the TEST A texture line, because the camera really is propped. Both test runs share that one still, so the video's last line is the only thing that changes.

## Script and voice memos

**DRAFT FOR CLIENT APPROVAL.** The reaction word is **optional**. If he'd rather not speak, R-01 is made silent (the no-word swap below), and the V03 stitch still carries his own voice. Until he approves a word, the prompts carry `[HIS APPROVED WORD, e.g. Twenty-five.]`.

**The question to send him** (he answers in a short memo, `MEMO_CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER_v09_interview.m4a`):
1. "When you saw September's calls in your report, what did you say, if anything? One or two words, the way you'd say it to yourself in the car."

We transcribe it and suggest one word or a very short phrase. He approves it in writing, then records it as its own memo.

| Shot | Starts at (in the clip) | Line shape (he decides) | Length | Memo file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v09_R-01_9x16` | second 5 | e.g. "Twenty-five." Said quietly, to himself, not to the camera | about 1 s, ends by second 6 | `MEMO_CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER_v09_line1.m4a` (+ `_car`) |

**Rules for his word:**
- The only number he may say is "twenty-five" (September), said as a word, exactly as the receipt shows.
- Never "best month since May", "since May", "first", "now", "just hit", "number one", "more", "up" or any growth word.
- No "Hulk did this" or "the agency got us": no causal line (G2, §1.5).
- A word that isn't a number ("Lovely.", "Look at that.") is fine too. The numbers stay on screen, from the receipt.

**How to record the memo (send this to him):**
- **Only after G3 clears.**
- One word or phrase per memo: three takes in the same file, with a 2-second gap between takes.
- Use a quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a lounge or bedroom (not the kitchen). No TV, radio or music.
- Hold the phone about **30 cm** from your mouth (production_rules A.3, as in V03), slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop.
- Use Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
- Say it the way you'd say it to yourself, quietly, not as if you're reading it out.
- **Then record it once more sitting in your parked car**, engine off, windows shut, phone in your dash mount about 55 cm away, and save it as `MEMO_CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER_v09_line1_car.m4a`. This gives us the real phone-in-a-car sound for the final track.
- Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. **Not WhatsApp.**
- Nobody's accent is ever described in a prompt. The memo carries the voice.

**Which memo goes where:** the clean indoor take is `@Audio 1` in Seedance, because it guides timbre and pace best. In the edit we lay in his real voice wherever sync allows (the `_car` take first). **If the generated voice doesn't sound like him, that is a QC fail** (production_rules G.1). Never ship a voice he hasn't heard and approved.

**Final 15 s timing (social cut, handles trimmed):**

| Edit time | Picture | Sound |
|---|---|---|
| 0.0–1.5 s | V03 stitch: his "…twenty-five" with the September tooltip on screen by 0.8 s | His V03 line (his real voice) |
| 1.5–9.0 s | `v09_R-01` (clip 0.5–8.0 s). Notification card 1.5–2.3 s | Rain on the roof, a soft notification ping at 1.5 s; the breath-laugh at about edit 5.0 s; **his word at about edit 6.0 s** |
| 9.0–13.0 s | `v09_B-01` (clip 0.5–4.5 s), the real tooltip keyed into the phone, then pushed to full frame | Cabin rain, the thumb swipe at about edit 10.5 s, a soft tick on the underline at 12.0 s |
| 13.0–15.0 s | End card | Ambience tail |

The phone upright on the top of the wheel in his right hand, the green screen clear with all four corners and dots visible, rain on the windscreen beyond, the camera almost still.

No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable. ### B1 · The owner films the real moment himself (real footage, not generated)

**Send him this:**
- **When:** the next time his monthly report arrives. Only when you are **parked at a kerb or on your drive with the engine off**. Never on a rank, and never while driving.
- **Set-up:** put your phone in your dash mount at chest height, front camera facing you. Use normal Video mode at 1080p, 30 fps. Portrait, Cinematic and beauty modes **off**. Seatbelt off. Wipe the lens.
- **Record:** start recording **before** you open the report. Then open it and read it as you normally would. Read it on a second phone or tablet; the recording phone stays in the mount the whole time. Keep the screen pointed at you, not at the camera. Let it run for 10 seconds after you've finished reading. 30–90 seconds is plenty.
- **Say whatever you'd naturally say, or nothing.** We only use the words you approve afterwards. If you read out a number, it must be from that report.
- **Keep it to you:** no passengers in the car, and no faces or number plates close to the windows.
- **Send us:**
  - The video at full size (AirDrop, Google Drive or email, **not WhatsApp**), named `grp_v09_R-01RF_t1_9x16.mov` (tell us which month's report it shows).
  - A screenshot of that month's Business Profile **Performance › Calls** page, plus a screenshot that shows the profile name, or the profile's share link. This also clears G3.
  - The report itself, if he's happy to share it, so we can match what he read.

**Honesty note (important):** "next month" means he will be reading the **October** report (or whichever month he films), not September's. We **never** put his real reaction to one month's report over another month's number. The receipts in the B1 cut come from the screenshot of the month he actually read, worded by the same rules. That means one period only, no "best month since…" and no growth words unless a comparison export proves them, and a part month is never called a drop. The title may change from "Twenty-Five" to that month's real figure. Tell us when he films, and we will rewrite the captions from the new screenshot.

**QC on his clip:** it is real, so it doesn't need realism checks. Check instead that the car is parked with the engine off, that no passenger, plate or house number is readable, that his reading screen doesn't show anyone else's personal data, and that he approves the words he used.

## What this video is

- **Concept.** Three short portraits from one wet October morning in the agency's real room. Each opens on the person's **hands** doing their real job (typing, sketching a report, making the tea), then a medium shot at **their own desk** where they say their name, their role and one true thing they do for a named client, then a small human tail (a laugh, a sip, back to work). It ends on **one real number** from a client they really worked on, shown as a receipt.
- **Hook.** Hands mid-task, with that person's receipt number on screen by **0.8 s** in the 9:16 cut.
- **Why this brand.** It is the agency itself, on its own service pages. It shows real people doing real work, which the 30 sample portraits on googlerankerpro.com can't do. Hassan comes last and is just another person at a desk: his hands-first shot is him making the tea.
- **What the edit reveals.** T1: **744** different searches Golden Line Taxis was shown for. T2: **25** calls from Google in September for Leam Taxis. Hassan: **312** clicks for Golden Line Taxis in three months (your pick; see the edit plan). Each is an exact crop of the real screenshot, with its source and dates.

**Hassan records the V10 wording ("co-founded"), not the draft in `founders.md` §7** ("I started Hulk Marketing").

**Rules for the lines**
- **T1's task** must come straight from the Golden Line work log, in about eight words, so the whole of line 2 takes 5 s or less. No causal verbs ("made", "drove", "got them to"), no rankings, no numbers.
- **T1's name:** say it in the form agreed in writing. If T1 is Muhammad Ali, agree a form that can't be confused with the "Ali" in Golden Line's duplicated reviews (G10), for example the full name.
- **No** "No.1", "first", "now", "last quarter" or growth words in any line.
- **"I make the tea"** stays only if it is true.
- Each memo is **one line**. Lines must be said in **5–6 s** at a natural pace. If a line runs longer, shorten the wording, not the pace.

**How to record a memo (send this to each person)**
- Use a quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a lounge or bedroom (not the kitchen or a stairwell). No TV, radio, fan or music. In Pakistan, turn the ceiling fan off.
- Hold the phone about **30 cm** from your mouth, slightly to one side, so your breath doesn't pop.
- Use Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
- **One line per memo.** Record three takes of the line, each as its own file: `MEMO_<CASTID>_v10_line<n>_t1.m4a`, `_t2`, `_t3`. We keep the best as `MEMO_<CASTID>_v10_line<n>.m4a`, trimmed to the line plus 0.3 s.
- Say it the way you'd say it to a colleague who asked, not as if reading.
- Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. **Not WhatsApp.**
- Nobody's accent is ever described in a prompt. The memo carries the voice.

**Which memo goes where.** The memo is the `@Audio` reference in Seedance (it guides timbre and pace), and we lay the real memo in as the final track wherever sync allows. **If the generated voice doesn't sound like the person, it fails QC** (production_rules G.1). Never publish a voice the person hasn't heard and approved.

## Version B fallback generations

**There are none to generate.** The plan's Version B for V10 is: *a person who won't appear is simply left out.* A meet-the-team clip of someone who isn't really on the team, or isn't really that person, would be a fake staff profile.

| Trigger | What happens | What you generate |
|---|---|---|
| T1, T2 or Hassan declines consent | Their clip is left out. The others still run in the same order, with Hassan last if he takes part | Nothing for that person |
| Someone consents to voice only, not likeness | Still left out of V10. The template needs their face at their desk, and the plan names no voice-only version | Nothing |
| Identity fails QC on every logged retry, and the person won't approve the result | Left out until a retry passes. Never publish a likeness the person hasn't approved | Nothing extra |
| G7: the Golden Line work log never arrives | T1's intro waits. We don't write a vaguer line 2, because "for Golden Line" still needs the log to be true | T1's hands shots only (they can wait in the drawer) |
| G3 fails, or T2 doesn't really build Leam Taxis' report | T2's line 2 and receipt switch to the client T2 really reports for, with that client's written permission and their real data. We rewrite both T2 intro prompts and the receipt, and you send the real screenshot if it isn't in `assets/gsc/` | The two T2 intros, from the rewritten prompts |

---

## What this video is

- **Concept.** An honest look behind the scenes. Every case study starts with no numbers, just a site map. The hands lead: a marker squeaks out an empty box and an arrow, blank Post-its go onto a monitor, and blank index cards are laid out like a family tree beside a green laptop. Then one medium-wide two-shot of T1 and T2 at the whiteboard: T2 draws, T1 points at a gap, a low wordless murmur, one laugh, and the kettle clicks off next door.
- **Hook (0–0.8 s).** The text card `Day one. No numbers yet.` is on screen from frame 1, over the first marker squeak.
- **Why this brand.** Zentro is not a taxi firm, so it widens the agency's story. It also has **no performance data on file at all**: no Search Console, no Business Profile, no rankings. That is exactly what "day one" looks like. The only real thing we can show is the structure of the site, and that structure is real: **10 laptop brands and 3 phone brands, each with its own repair page.**
- **What the edit reveals.** The green laptop gets Zentro's real brand-repair page, keyed in from today's capture. We push into the screen, and the real brand grids fill the frame. Each brand tile is outlined one by one, then the card reads `10 laptop brands · 3 phone brands · a page each`, with the source line and the context `No performance data yet.` The film ends on `Ask us again in three months.`

**Deviations from the plan (one line each):**
- **Shooting order** is O-02 → O-03 → O-01 → O-04 (the shot needing no consent goes first, then the work is batched by set-up: desk, then whiteboard). The gen IDs don't change.
- **Hands-only twins `O-01C` and `O-03C` are added** (Version B), because the plan gives O-01 to T2's hand and O-03 to T1's hands. The twins are anonymous Mode C hands, so the hands-only cut can be made today with no consent.
- **O-02's monitor is switched off** (a dark matte screen with no picture) instead of SCREEN-SOFT. A phone 35 cm from a bezel keeps the screen in sharp focus, so a "soft" screen would be physically wrong. A switched-off matte screen gives the same result: no readable detail.
- **TEXT-LOCK is added to O-03** (production_rules §F asks for it in every prompt with a place). O-02 keeps the plan's PAL-INT without the AGENCY ADD-ON, because its orange Post-its already carry the orange.
- **L-OFFICE is adapted in the three hands shots** ("the right side of the hand and the board fall a stop darker"), because there is no face in frame. It is verbatim in O-04.
- **The laptop insert is the real brand grid, static, not a scroll of `now_desktop_full.png`.** That homepage shows the banned Zentro self-claims (5,000+ customers, 4.8/5, 2,560+ reviews) and the unsourced testimonials. Also, no hand touches the laptop in O-03, so a scroll would look like it moved on its own.
- **The receipts come from the brand grids** on zentro.co.uk/laptop-repair and /mobile-repair. We captured them today, 22 Oct 2026. They print each brand's name and the site's own counts, "10 brands available" and "3 brands available". The open navigation-menu captures are kept as alternates. The source line now names those pages.
- **The Google "G" logo** in Zentro's mobile grid: two options, your choice. **(a)** Leave the tile untouched: it is the site's own mark, kept as evidence (§1.2). **(b)** Desaturate the logo area to grey, so no Google colours show (§9 "no Google marks"). Either way the word "Google" stays. We default to (b) unless you tell us otherwise.
- **Hands-only stills use Nano Banana Pro, not Soul** (team.md §5 gives Soul to solo anchor stills): there is no face to lock, and Nano Banana Pro follows the hand, desk and screen detail more closely.
- **The O-04 label drops "Their words, their voice."** Nobody says any words in V11, so that part of the §1.3 label wouldn't be true.
- **The anonymous version says "a UK repair business", not "a Manchester repair business".** Zentro publishes no address; Manchester is only inferred from its 0161 number.
- **The Golden Line fallback counts come from today's captures:** 17 location pages and 8 airport pages. The live menu lists "Hampton Airport Taxi" twice (Hampton Lucy and Hampton Magna), so Golden Line fixes that label before we use the capture (G11).

### The set (the same in every shot)
- **The room:** an ordinary small office with pale grey walls and a large window on the left wall: rain on the glass, a grey sky, and a plain white roller blind hanging slightly crooked. A radiator, and a kettle within earshot.
- **The desk:** a worn wood-effect top with a dark keyboard and a monitor on a plain grey stand. A **plain dark grey 14-inch laptop** with no stickers (the same laptop as V08), and a white charging cable over the desk edge.
- **The orange enamel mug with the small chipped rim:** the agency's one brand-orange object, plain, hot tea, steaming. It sits at a frame edge in O-01, O-03 and O-04.
- **The whiteboard:** plain white, slightly worn, with faint shapeless smudges of old marker. It has an aluminium frame and pen tray, a grey felt eraser, and **plain dark markers with nothing printed on the barrel** (peel or tape over the label if you're shooting real reference photos). **Only empty boxes and arrows ever go on it: no words, no letters, no numbers, no client names.**
- **Sticky notes:** blank, square, pale yellow and orange. **Index cards:** plain white, unruled, blank.

## Script and voice memos

**No dialogue, no voice-over and no memos.** The only voices in V11 are an **unintelligible murmur and one laugh** in `O-04`, generated with the picture. Any intelligible word in any clip fails QC. Nobody records anything.

**Who approves what:**
- **T1 and T2:** how they are shown (O-04), their first names in the label, that the whiteboard scene reflects how they really work, and that they really work on the Zentro audit (or, in B2, the Golden Line audit).
- **T1 and T2, sound:** hear and approve O-04's generated murmur and laugh before release. If either says no, we mute the native voices and lay in a real wordless murmur recorded in the room.
- **Zentro:** being named, and the brand-page capture on screen (G2).
- **You:** the end line, the brand lockup, and the date of day one.

**Every word on screen is edit text**, added by us. These are the exact words:

| When | Text |
|---|---|
| 0.0–2.4 s (hook card) | `Day one. No numbers yet.` |
| 11.0–15.4 s (receipt card) | `10 laptop brands · 3 phone brands · a page each` |
| 11.0–15.4 s (source line) | `zentro.co.uk · laptop and mobile repair pages · captured 22 Oct 2026` |
| 14.2–15.4 s (context strip) | `No performance data yet.` |
| 17.4–20.0 s (end line) | `Ask us again in three months.` |
| 0.0–15.4 s (label) | `Illustrative footage. Real data.` |
| 15.4–20.0 s (label) | `AI re-creation made with [Name] and [Name]'s permission. Real data.` |
| 19.4–20.0 s (end card) | Your brand lockup (Hulk Marketing, or "Hulk Marketing · part of Google Ranker Pro") |

**Numbers** appear only as the site's own printed counts on the real crops, and in the card above. Nobody speaks them.

> **If a later version adds a spoken line** (for example T1 saying the end line), it follows the team memo method: one line per memo, three takes, a quiet room with soft furnishings, the phone about 30 cm from the mouth, lossless or 44.1/48 kHz mono, numbers said as words, and the file named `MEMO_T1_SEO_v11_line1.m4a`. It is not needed for this cut.

No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
The laptop screen shows a flat, uniform, matte chroma-green fill from edge to edge, evenly lit, with no interface, no text, no reflections and no glare; all four corners and the bezel stay visible, with one small dark dot in each corner of the green. The screen gives off almost no light.
The index cards are plain white and completely blank on both sides; the laptop has no logo and no stickers; the orange enamel mug is plain, with no print.
Exactly one person visible, seen only as two hands and forearms; no face and no reflection of a face anywhere. No extra people.
Filmed handheld on a smartphone main camera: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.
```

- **QC (pass/fail):** the same as O-03, except identity.
  - **Screen keyable.** Flat green with four dots; camera static. *Fail:* region edit: `EDIT TARGET: Edit @Video 1, seconds X-Y only. CHANGE: the laptop screen becomes a flat, uniform, matte chroma-green fill with one small dark dot in each corner; no interface, no glare. PROTECT: the hands, the cards, the mug and steam, the camera, the light and the sound; everything else unchanged.`
  - **Cards are paper and blank.** *Fail (floaty):* drop the 5–6 s hold. *If marks appear:* region edit them blank.
  - **Hands anonymous and correct.** Five fingers, the chipped thumbnail, mid-blue cuffs, no ring, watch or tattoo. *Fail:* attach `REF_HANDS_C_08.jpg` to the still and remake it.
  - **Real-life look.** *Fail (game render):* remake the still; then add `No game-engine look, no CG gloss.` after the light line.

## Edit plan (what we do after hand-back)

**Nothing is published until** Hulk's role on Zentro and permission to name it are confirmed in writing (G2), you've confirmed day one is real (see the gates), and, if O-04 is in the cut, T1 and T2 have approved it with its sound. If either answer is no, we cut B2 or B3 from the same clips. **No credit line** ("we built", "Website by", "our client") appears in the Zentro version: the film shows the start of an audit, not a result.

**Before-and-after:** none. V11 is day one, so there is no "before" to compare, and **no Wayback captures are needed** for it. For the honest follow-up the end line promises ("Ask us again in three months"), we need two things now: **the audit start date**, and **Search Console access for zentro.co.uk from day one**. Then the three-month video has a dated baseline and a real Compare export, not an estimate.

**Receipt grammar (master_plan §1.2):**
- **Crops:** exact crops of our dated captures, never redrawn or re-typed, on a navy `#0B1628` card with a 12 px radius.
- **Highlights:** thin orange `#F7931E` outlines (2 px) go round each brand tile one at a time. There is no counter animation and no number counts up: the only numbers are the site's own printed counts, underlined once.
- **Movement:** a slow push from 102% to 108%, or a slow drift across the wider grid, with grain matched to the phone footage.
- **If you choose Hulk Marketing for social:** outlines, underlines and lockup switch to Hulk lime `#C6FA61`, and the card to `#121C17`.

### Sound, captions, labels, loudness, finishing

- **Native sound** stays and carries the film: squeaks, paper, card taps, the murmur and laugh, the kettle click, rain and room tone. Use 4-frame crossfades at every cut so the rain never jumps. Add soft ticks only on the underlines (and one per grid).
- **Music:** none by default, because the foley is the rhythm. If you want a bed, use one sparse licensed track (no vocals, no trending or copyrighted audio), at least 20 LU under the foley so the squeaks stay on top, out by 19.4.
- **Captions:** there are no spoken words, so there are no word captions. The text cards carry the story. If a platform needs captions, the only entries are `[marker squeaks]`, `[indistinct murmur]`, `[laughs]` and `[kettle clicks off]`.
- **Disclosure:** labels small, lower-left, on throughout (as above). Platform toggles on every post: TikTok AIGC, YouTube altered or synthetic content, Meta AI info. You and your adviser sign off the wording.
- **9:16 safe zones:** all text between 12% and 80% of the height (y 230–1536 of 1920), with 60 px side margins.
- **Loudness:** −14 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP.
- **Screen key (O-03):**
  - corner-pin on the four dots;
  - insert at about 85% white with a slight cool cast;
  - a soft glare pass from the window side (left);
  - a 1–2 px chromatic edge and faint moiré (a phone filming a laptop), plus a grain match;
  - motion matched to the colleague's breathing micro-shake.
- **Finishing:** one grain value, one sharpen value and one light grade across all clips (lift the shadows a touch; never teal-and-orange). Upscale once with Higgsfield `upscale_video` (ugc preset), only if you had to generate at 720p.
- **Never on screen:** "No.1", "#1", "first", "now" as a claim, "growth", "+%", up-arrows or count-ups. Also never: Zentro's 5,000+ / 4.8/5 / 2,560+ claims or any of its testimonials; "we built", "Website by" or "our client" for Zentro; any "Ali"; clock or time stamps; Google logos or colours on our graphics.

## What this video is

- **Concept.** One real month-end for T2, the reporting lead, in five beats: arrive, pull the export, check the number twice, call the client, log off. Two selfie beats (morning at the door, evening at the desk) bookend three phone b-roll beats. It is filmed only at the place you confirm (UK or Pakistan), with only details that are true of that place and that person.
- **Hook.** Frame 1 is T2's selfie at the door, coat on, saying "Month-end." The real "25" tooltip sits as a small receipt in the corner by 0.8 s.
- **Why this brand.** Leam Taxis' Business Profile shows **25 calls in September 2026**, read exactly from the tooltip. It is the best of the six months on the chart. A September report is where that number lands, and the report T2 sends here is the one the owner opens in V09. Hulk owns the story because it is about the work (building and sending the report), not about a result claim.
- **What the edit reveals.** At about 10 s, the real Leam Taxis calls chart is keyed into the green laptop screen and the September tooltip is ringed as T2's finger stops. At about 24 s, as T2 says "twenty-five", the real tooltip appears as a full receipt: `25 calls from Google in September`, with its source line. The end card reads `Watch the client open it →` and links to V09.

**Changes from the plan (one line each):**
- **Chart crop:** the plan calls `15,165,910,310` "the chart crop", but gsc_story §4 lists that as headline + chart (it shows "114" without its range). On the laptop we key the chart-only crop `15,265,910,210`, so a six-month total never appears inside a September story without its range. The September tooltip sits inside it.
- **`A-02` is a controlled two-shot** with one hard cut at second 3: the kettle and the desk are two places, and one 6 s take cannot travel between them. If T2's desk really is in the kitchen, tell us and we make it one take.
- **`A-03`, `A-04` and `B-02` stand on a shelf.** CAMERA says static, and the last line is the verbatim PHONE-REAR line, as the plan's own static rear-camera shots do (§8.3, V01's `BR01_9x16`). Only if a take sways, retry once with `propped on a stand` in place of `handheld` (one variable, logged).
- **`A-03` keeps T2's head out of frame** (shoulder, arm and hands only), so the same clip works unchanged in Version B, which the plan builds from `A-02` and `A-03`.
- **`A-03` optics:** the PHONE-REAR block says 1–2 m. Here it is about 70 cm, because the phone stands on the shelf just behind the shoulder.
- **`A-04`:** T2 holds the call phone to the ear on the window side, the side away from the camera, so the mouth stays visible for lip-sync. The camera is a second phone on the shelf.
- **`A-05`:** the selfie phone is in T2's **left** hand, so the right hand can reach the desk lamp at screen-left. That lamp is the camera-left key in L-HOME.
- **The coat** is the add-on line from `pack/characters/team.md` §8 (our addition), and it is used only if T2 really wears a coat.
- **Version B gets three new hands-only generations** (`B-01` door, `B-02` call at the window, `B-03` lamp off). `A-02` and `A-03` alone give about 10 s of usable picture, which is not enough for a 30 s cut. They are not in the count.
- **The payoff lands at about 24 s (80%)**, as the plan sets it, which is later than the 60–70% social rule. The keyed chart at about 10 s carries the first reveal.

**Agency draft. T2 edits, approves and records each line.** Only the approved words go into the prompts. If T2 changes a word, tell us and we update the prompts before you generate.

| `v12_A-05_9x16` | second 1, ends by second 6 | "Report's sent. Twenty-five calls from Google in September. Logging off." | about 5 s | `MEMO_T2_REPORTING_v12_line3.m4a` (+ `_desk`) |

**Rules for the lines:**
- **Line 2 is one side of a call only.** The client's voice is never heard and never generated.
- **"Morning."** stays only if the call really happens in the morning. **"In your inbox"** stays only if the report really goes by email. Otherwise T2 says what is true, for example "Your report's just gone over."
- **The only number spoken is "twenty-five"**, said as words, and it must match the receipt (September 2026).
- **Never add:** "He'll ring me in about ten minutes", "a hundred and fourteen since May", "best month since May", "number one", "first", "just hit", "up", "more", or any line saying Hulk caused the calls.
- **T2 does not name the client on camera.** The receipt names Leam Taxis only with their written OK.

**How to record each memo (send this to T2):**
- **One line per memo:** three takes in the same file, with a 2-second gap between takes.
- **Room:** a quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a bedroom or lounge (not the kitchen or a stairwell). No TV, radio or music. Turn any fan off.
- **Phone:** about **30 cm** from your mouth (production_rules A.3, as in V10 and T2's character file), slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop. Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
- **Delivery:** say it the way you would really say it, not as if reading. Your own accent; nobody ever describes it in a prompt.
- **Then one "real place" take of each line** for the final track: line 1 on the front camera at arm's length **at the real door** (`_door`); line 2 standing at the real window with your phone at your ear and a second phone recording from the shelf (`_room`); line 3 at the desk on the front camera at arm's length (`_desk`).
- Name the files `MEMO_T2_REPORTING_v12_line<n>_t1.m4a`, `_t2`, `_t3`, plus `_door`, `_room`, `_desk`. We keep the best take as `MEMO_T2_REPORTING_v12_line<n>.m4a`. Send full size by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. **Not WhatsApp.**

**Which memo goes where:** the clean indoor take is `@Audio 1` in Seedance, because it guides timbre and pace best. In the edit we lay in the real-place take (`_door`, `_room`, `_desk`) wherever sync allows. **If the generated voice doesn't sound like T2, that is a QC fail** (production_rules G.1). Never ship a voice T2 hasn't heard and approved.

```
ASSET MAP
@Image 1: identity of the reporting lead (face, hair, build, wardrobe: a navy knit jumper with the sleeves pushed up, plain dark trousers; no logos, no printed text; their own plain dark coat, open, over the same). 100% matches the reference.
@Image 2: the same person on a smartphone front camera at arm's length; identity and front-camera face proportions only; do not copy its background or its light.
@Image 3: anchor still for this shot: framing, light direction, wardrobe and the doorway layout in frame one; frame one matches this; do not copy any text.
@Image 4: geography and materials of the real entrance only (door, frame, wall, downpipe); do not copy its camera angle; ignore any house number, street name, letterbox lettering or sign in it.
@Audio 1: the reporting lead's own voice for the line at second 1 only; ignore its background noise.

SCENE CONTEXT
On a grey, drizzly late-October morning, a reporting lead stands on the step outside the door where their working day starts and records a short selfie clip on their phone. They say one line to the phone, then lean back against the door and let it swing open behind them.

LOCATION MAP
Camera: the phone's front camera in the reporting lead's outstretched right hand, about 45 centimetres from the face, slightly above eye level, pointing back at them and at the entrance behind them. Foreground: only fine drizzle between the lens and the face. Midground: the reporting lead on the step, head and shoulders in the middle of the vertical frame. Background, mostly in focus: the closed door directly behind them, its lever handle at their left hip, just out of frame at the lower right; the wet wall at screen-left with a downpipe running down it; the corner of the neighbour's wet brickwork at the screen-left edge; the top of a wheelie bin half-cropped at the lower-left corner, its lid not quite shut; a cobweb beaded with drizzle in the top corner of the door frame. Behind the door, unseen until it opens: a dim hallway.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains the reporting lead; no empty establishing frame. Head and shoulders fill the middle of the vertical frame, a little left of centre, the top of the head nearly touching the top edge. Torso faces the lens; eyes on the screen image of themselves; lips closed. The left hand hangs loose at their side, out of frame. The coat hangs open, drizzle beads on its shoulders.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
About 80° diagonal field of view, phone front-camera perspective, lens 40 to 55 cm from the face at arm's length, slightly above eye level. The face sits close and slightly enlarged at the centre, background visible to the frame edges and mostly in focus, straight lines stay straight, no portrait bokeh.

CAMERA
The phone is held in the speaker's own outstretched right hand; the frame moves with their arm: slight handheld micro-shake, small drifts with their breathing and as they turn their head, a natural re-grip once.
Their eyes flick between the lens and the screen image of themselves, as people do on a front camera.
Framing is casual and a little off-centre; the top of the head is nearly touching the top of the frame.
Auto exposure breathes slightly when the frame swings towards the dim hallway at second 6, then settles.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. The reporting lead lifts the phone the last few centimetres into place, re-grips it once and takes a small breath; a faint puff of vapour leaves the mouth. End state: lips parted, about to speak, eyes on the screen image.
1-6s: At second 1, @Image 1 the reporting lead says, in natural British English, "Month-end. One of my taxi clients. Let's see what September did.", brisk and plain, a small lift of the eyebrows on "September". Mid-line they glance once off to screen-left and back to the screen image. The free hand stays down, out of frame, away from the mouth. End state: lips closed, a small half-smile, eyes on the screen image.
6-8s: At second 6 their left hand reaches behind them to the lever handle and presses it down; they lean back with the left shoulder and the door swings inward behind them; the frame tips a few degrees and swings with their arm, and the dim hallway opens up behind their shoulder. At second 7 the door slows and stops against its own weight. End state: standing on the step, the door open behind them, the hallway dim behind their shoulder; ambience only.

PHYSICS
The door has real weight: the lever resists, then gives with a clunk; the door swings on its hinges with a slight drag of the seal and slows on its own. Their shoulder takes the door's weight; the coat bunches where it presses and slides back as they move. Drizzle beads sit on the coat and hair and do not move with the camera.

LIGHTING
Flat overcast sky as a huge soft source from above; soft shadows under the eyes and chin; wet tarmac reflects the grey sky; no direct sun. As the door opens, the hallway behind is dimmer, lit only by the grey daylight coming through the doorway.
Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched.
Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each, fingers not touching the face during speech.

AUDIO
Ambience: fine drizzle on the pavement, a gutter dripping onto the step, a car hissing past on the wet road, distant traffic.
Foley: a coat rustle and a soft grip noise on the phone at 0 seconds; the lever handle clunk at 6 seconds; the door's hinge creak and the seal brushing the frame at 6 to 7 seconds.

## What this video is

- **Concept.** A sit-down documentary interview with Hassan at his real desk by a rainy window, deliberately not his black-studio portrait look. He says who Hulk helps, why he started it, what clients actually get every month, and what he will never promise. The human story comes first; the receipts land at 34 s: the Companies House record, then a 6 s montage of three real client receipts on his green laptop.
- **Hook.** 16:9: Hassan walking in out of the rain at his real building, shaking and folding an umbrella; his first line lands on the cut to the interview. 9:16: a selfie cold open in drizzle in the car park: "If you run a local business and people can't find you on Google, this is why we exist."
- **Why this brand.** It is the homepage hero for googlerankerpro.com. It puts a real, named founder in a real room, which the five polished AI service presenters on the site can't do, and it matches the site's own line "No ranking guarantees".
- **What the edit reveals.** `Hulk Marketing Ltd · company no. 15931335 · incorporated 2 Sep 2024` (Companies House), then Golden Line's **744** different searches, Leam Taxis' **114** calls May–Oct 2026 (October part month) and Coventry's **79** Business Profile interactions May–Oct 2026. It closes on "No ranking guarantees." over Hassan picking up a buzzing phone at the window.

## Script and voice memos

**How the words are made.** We send Hassan the four questions. He answers them in one relaxed **10-minute voice memo** (`MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v13_interview.m4a`), the way he'd talk to a client. We transcribe it and cut it into short lines (drafts below where the plan has them). He edits and approves each line **in writing**, then records each approved line on its own. Only approved words go into a prompt.

- **Q1** Who do you help, in one sentence?
- **Q2** Why did you start it?
- **Q3** What does a client actually get from you every month?
- **Q4** What will you never promise?
- **Cold open** (9:16 only) If you run a local business and people can't find you on Google, why do you exist?

| Memo file | Shot · starts at | Line (DRAFT until he approves it) | Must end by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v13_line1.m4a` | `v13_A-01` · second 1 | "Taxi firms, a fostering agency, local businesses where one phone call matters." | second 7 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v13_line2.m4a` | `v13_A-01` · second 8 | [APPROVED LINE 2 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT, Q1]. Draft to react to: "Good at what they do, and hard to find when someone searches." | second 13 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v13_line3.m4a` | `v13_A-02` · second 1 | [APPROVED LINE 3 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT, Q2: his real reason, first half] | second 6 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v13_line4.m4a` | `v13_A-02` · second 7 | [APPROVED LINE 4 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT, Q2: his real reason, second half] | second 12 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v13_line5.m4a` | `v13_A-03` (both ratios) · second 1 | "Every month you get your own Google numbers." | second 6 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v13_line6.m4a` | `v13_A-03` (both ratios) · second 7 | "The good months and the quiet ones, with the context next to them." | second 12 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v13_line7.m4a` | `v13_A-04` · second 1 | "A ranking. No ranking guarantees. Just the work, and the real numbers." | second 7 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v13_line8.m4a` | `v13_S-01` · second 1 | "If you run a local business and people can't find you on Google, this is why we exist." | second 8 |

**Rules for the lines**
- **No numbers are spoken.** The numbers are ours, on screen as receipts. If his real reason (Q2) includes a number or a year, it must be true and written as words, and we check it before he records.
- **Each line is said in 5–6 s at a natural pace** (about 12–14 words). If a line runs longer, shorten the words, not the pace.
- Never "No.1", "first", "now", "growth", "last quarter", "guaranteed results" or a causal verb (made, drove, caused).
- Clients stay unnamed in the lines. Only "No ranking guarantees" is presented as the site's own line.
- Q2 is his real reason. We don't write it for him; lines 3 and 4 stay placeholders until he approves his own words.

**How to record a memo (send this to Hassan)**
- A quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a lounge or bedroom (not a kitchen or stairwell). No TV, radio, fan or music.
- Hold the phone about **30 cm** from your mouth, slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop.
- Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
- **One line per file:** three takes in the same file with a 2-second gap between them. We keep the best take, trimmed to the line plus 0.3 s, as the file name in the table.
- Say it the way you'd say it to a client on the phone, not as if reading.
- **Line 8** twice: once indoors as above, and once outdoors in the car park on the phone, held at arm's length (`MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v13_line8_outdoor.m4a`). The outdoor one is the backup for the selfie's sound and the voice for Version B's 9:16 cold open.
- Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. **Not WhatsApp.**
- His accent is never described in any prompt. The memo carries the voice.

**Which memo goes where.** Each memo is the `@Audio` reference in its Seedance shot (it guides timbre and pace), and we lay the real memo in as the final track wherever sync allows. **If the generated voice doesn't sound like Hassan, the clip fails QC** (production_rules G.1). Nothing he hasn't heard and approved is published.

**Before pasting any Seedance prompt with a line:** replace the quoted words with his **approved** words exactly, keeping the start second. Lines 2, 3 and 4 are placeholders until then.

47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens character, camera 2 to 3 metres from the subject, natural human-eye perspective, zero obvious distortion, natural face proportions, background readable but softly out of focus.

0-1s: Ambience only. He sits settled and takes a small breath in. End state: lips parted, about to speak, eyes on the interviewer.

7-8s: A short pause: he shifts his weight in the chair and his eyes drop briefly towards the window side to think, then come back to the interviewer. End state: lips parted again.

The chair takes his weight and creaks as he shifts at second 7; the suit jacket bunches at the elbow on the armrest and smooths again as he moves; his shirt cuff slides back a little as the hand lifts; when his fingers meet the mug handle the mug nudges a centimetre across the table and the steam bends; the umbrella and the coat stay exactly where they are.

## What this video is

- **Concept.** A weekly 30-second tip from Hassan, filmed on his own phone on a little desk tripod: the same desk, framing and jumper every week, so it reads as a real habit. In the edit we cut him out of his real room with a matte (the "green-screen effect", no physical green screen) and put the real Search Console row behind him in the top third. He points up at it.
- **Hook.** A myth line in the first second ("Myth: you need more content to rank. Usually you don't."), with the receipt `taxi warwick · 665 times shown · avg 10.7` behind him by 0.8 s.
- **The tip.** Find a search with lots of impressions sitting around position ten, then fix the page you already have (title, local proof, links from your other pages) instead of writing a new blog.
- **Why this brand.** Golden Line is the one client where the agency credit is verified (live footer "Made with ❤ by Hulk Marketing Ltd"), and its row 5 is a textbook "edge of page one" case: shown 665 times at an average position of 10.7 with a 0.9% click-through. V15 later reports the whole Warwick cluster.
- **What the edit reveals.** Golden Line's real row 5 (`goldenlinetaxiswarwick_gsc_3m.png`, 19 Jul–18 Oct 2026): 6 clicks, 665 impressions, 0.9% CTR, position 10.7, with the source line and "average position" context on screen.

## Script and voice memos

**Agency draft.** Hassan edits it, approves it **in writing**, then records each approved line on its own. Numbers are said as words, exactly as written. If he rewords a line, the numbers stay exactly as they are.

| Memo file | Shot · starts at | Line (DRAFT until he approves it) | Must end by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v14_line1.m4a` | `v14_A-01` · second 1 | "Myth: you need more content to rank. Usually you don't." | second 5 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v14_line2.m4a` | `v14_A-01` · second 5 | "Find a search with loads of impressions sitting around position ten." | second 9 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v14_line3.m4a` | `v14_A-02` · second 1 | "One Warwick taxi firm. The search: taxi warwick. Shown six hundred and sixty-five times in three months, averaging ten point seven." | second 8 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v14_line4.m4a` | `v14_A-02` · second 8 | "That's the edge of page one, and fewer than one in a hundred got a click." | second 13 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v14_line5.m4a` | `v14_A-03` · second 1 | "Don't write a new blog. Fix the page that's already there: the title, local proof, links from your other pages." | second 8 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v14_line6.m4a` | `v14_A-03` · second 9 (**optional**) | "That's the one we're on next." **Only if the Golden Line work log confirms it (G7).** | second 11 |

**Where every number comes from:** `goldenlinetaxiswarwick_gsc_3m.png` row 5, crop `24, 1100, 1318, 49`: "taxi warwick", 6 clicks, 665 impressions, 0.9% CTR, position 10.7, window 19 Jul–18 Oct 2026 ("three months"). 6 ÷ 665 = 0.9%, so "fewer than one in a hundred" is true.

**Rules for the lines**
- Impressions are "times shown", never "people saw" or "people searched".
- 10.7 is an **average** position: "averaging ten point seven", "the edge of page one". Never "page one", "No.1", "first", "now", "just hit", "last quarter" or a causal verb (made, drove, caused).
- Each line is one memo at his natural pace: lines 1 and 2 about 3–4 s, line 3 about 6–7 s, line 4 about 5 s, line 5 about 7 s, line 6 about 2 s. If a line runs long, cut words, not pace.

**How to record a memo (send this to Hassan)**
- A quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a lounge or bedroom (not a kitchen or stairwell). No TV, radio, fan or music.
- Hold the phone about **30 cm** from your mouth, slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop.
- Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
- **One line per file:** three takes in the same file with a 2-second gap between them. We keep the best take, trimmed to the line plus 0.3 s, and send it back to you under the file name in the table. Upload only that trimmed one-take file as @Audio, never the raw three-take recording.
- Say it the way you'd explain it to a client across the desk, not as if reading.
- Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. **Not WhatsApp.**
- His accent is never described in any prompt. The memo carries the voice.

**Which memo goes where.** Each memo is the `@Audio` reference in its Seedance shot (it guides timbre and pace), and we lay the real memo in as the final track wherever sync allows. **If the generated voice doesn't sound like Hassan, the clip fails QC** (production_rules G.1). Nothing he hasn't heard and approved is published.

**Before pasting any Seedance prompt with a line:** replace the quoted words with his **approved** words exactly, keeping the start second.

**Version B (T1):** we send T1 the same five lines. T1 edits, approves and records three takes of each line as team.md §7 describes (`MEMO_T1_SEO_v14_line<n>_t1.m4a`, `_t2`, `_t3`); we send back the best takes, trimmed, as `MEMO_T1_SEO_v14_line1.m4a` to `_line5.m4a`.

## Edit plan (what we do after hand-back)

**Shape (30 s, 9:16, 1080×1920).** Three talking takes, hard cuts, the 1 s handles trimmed so frame 1 is his first word. Timings below are for planned takes; we re-time to the real ones.

| Final cut | Source | What's on screen |
|---|---|---|
| 0.0–8.8 s | `A-01` 1.0–9.8 s | 0.0 first word. **By 0.8 s:** the matte is on and the receipt card is in the top third behind him, with our caption above it: `taxi warwick · 665 times shown · avg 10.7`. Word captions: "Myth: you need more content to rank." / "Usually you don't." At 4.0 s he points up and back; the card gets a slow 102% → 108% push-in. At "position ten" (about 7.8 s) a soft tick and the orange underline draws under **10.7**. Reframes: 105% at about 2.6 s ("Usually you don't"), back to 100% at 4.0 s for the point, 105% at 6.0 s |
| 8.8–20.6 s | `A-02` 1.0–12.8 s | Hard cut with a 105% punch-in; ease back to 100% at about 11.0 s; 105% at 13.0 s. The card becomes the **header + top-5 block** (column names visible), rows 1–4 dimmed to 40% so row 5 reads. Underline under **665** on "six hundred and sixty-five" (about 11.8 s), then under **10.7** on "ten point seven" (about 14.8 s), when the context strip appears. At the lean (about 15.8 s) a punch-in to 108%. On "fewer than one in a hundred" (about 18.8 s) the underline moves to **0.9%** and a small caption reads `6 clicks from 665 times shown` |
| 20.6–29.6 s | `A-03` 1.0–10.0 s | Hard cut in at 105%; 100% at 22.6 s; 105% at 25.0 s ("local proof"); 100% at 28.6 s for the reach. 20.6–22.6 s the **full-width row** slides across the top band at 1.6× and pans from the query to the position cell (the proof that the cells come from one row). Then a typed list builds on each finger: `1 The title` / `2 Local proof` / `3 Links from your other pages`. From 22.6 s the typed list replaces the hook card in the top band (300–640 px), one item per finger; word captions pause during the count (the list carries the words) and return for the reach. At the reach (about 28.6 s) the end card rises over the frame shiver; the fingertip tap is the last sound |
| 29.6–30.0 s | last frame held | End card |

**The receipt (master_plan §1.2, edit-only, never redrawn).** All crops are from `assets/gsc/goldenlinetaxiswarwick_gsc_3m.png` (1366×2251), on a navy `#0B1628` card with a 12 px radius, one thin orange `#F7931E` underline under one figure at a time, a soft tick SFX on each underline, a slow 102% → 108% push-in and a grain match to the footage.

| Card | Crop (x, y, w, h) | Shows | Used |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hook card, header | `840, 847, 502, 57` | Clicks · Impressions · CTR · Position (the real header cells; this rectangle was checked on the PNG) | stacked directly above the figures crop, same scale |
| Hook card, top | `24, 1100, 300, 49` | Row 5 query cell: "taxi warwick" | 0.0–8.8 s only (from 22.6 s the typed list holds the top band; the source line leaves with the card and returns under the full row in the end card) |
| Hook card, bottom | `840, 1100, 502, 49` | Row 5 figures: 6 · 665 · 0.9% · 10.7 | the same. The two pieces are from the same row, stacked with a visible 12 px gap; only the blank middle of the row is left out |
| Header + top 5, query column | `24, 847, 300, 303` | "Top queries" and rows 1–5 | 8.8–20.6 s, left |
| Header + top 5, figures | `840, 847, 502, 303` | Clicks, Impressions, CTR, Position and rows 1–5 | 8.8–20.6 s, right, with a thin gap between the two |
| Full row 5 | `24, 1100, 1318, 49` | The whole row, unaltered | 20.6–22.6 s pan, and in the end card |

Why split: the full row at 1080 px wide shrinks its text to about 10 px, which nobody can read on a phone. The cell crops scale to about 23 px. Nothing is re-typed; the column labels come from the real header.

**Exact on-screen wording.**
- Hook caption (by 0.8 s): `taxi warwick · 665 times shown · avg 10.7`
- Source line (always on under the card, Inter 500, `#BDCBDC`): `Google Search Console · goldenlinetaxiswarwick.co.uk · 19 Jul–18 Oct 2026`
- Context strip (from 14.8 s): `Average position, Google Search Console, 19 Jul–18 Oct 2026.` and, on the next line, `Positions 1–10 are page one.`
- Permission line in the end card, once Golden Line agrees: `Shared with Golden Line Taxis' permission.`
- Never on screen: "people saw", "people searched", "No.1", "#1", "first", "now", "just hit", "growth", "+x%", up-arrows, "last quarter", count-ups, Google logos or Google colours on our graphics.

**The green-screen effect (no physical green screen).** A per-frame segmentation matte (DaVinci Magic Mask, After Effects Roto Brush or Runway) cuts him out of his real room. The real room stays behind everything, dimmed by about 35% and slightly softened, so it is still visibly his office. The receipt card sits between the room and him in the top third, angled about 4°, its lower edge just above his raised finger at 4.0 s. A 2 px light-wrap from the window side and the same grain on both layers. If the matte chatters on his hair against the window, we keep the card a little lower so his head overlaps it less.

**Before and after.** **None in Ep 1.** The tip is about fixing a page that already exists, and we have no "after" for it yet. Nothing is needed from Wayback for this episode. (When a later episode shows a page before and after a fix, the "before" is a real dated capture you make in your own browser, as in `research/wayback_before.md`; the archive refused our connection.)

**Captions.** Word-timed, Inter, white with a soft shadow, two lines at most, in the band from about 1250 to 1440 px (on his chest, below his chin). Numbers in captions as on the receipt: 665, 10.7, 0.9%. Captions match his words exactly; where he says "impressions", the receipt caption already reads "times shown".

**9:16 safe zones.** Top 12% (0–230 px) and bottom 20% (1536–1920 px) stay clear of all text. Series chip `Tip of the Week · Ep 1` at about 240–280 px (Version B: a name/role chip `[Full name] · SEO Specialist, Hulk Marketing` directly under the series chip, from 0.0 to 3.0 s), receipt card about 300–640 px, captions about 1250–1440 px, disclosure label just above 1536 px.

**Disclosure label** (persistent, small, lower-left above the safe zone; you and your adviser confirm the wording): `AI re-creation made with Hassan Pasha's permission. Their words, their voice. Real data.` Version B: the same with T1's full name. Set the TikTok AIGC toggle, YouTube "altered or synthetic content" and Meta "AI info" on every post.

**Sound.** Keep Seedance's room tone, rain and foley. Lay in Hassan's real memos as the final voice wherever sync holds (checked frame by frame). A soft tick on each underline; the real fingertip tap at the end. No music under the first line; we suggest no bed at all for this series (the rain and room are the texture). If you want one, it is one sparse licensed bed, the same every week, at least 20 LU under speech, never trending or copyrighted audio. Master at **−14 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP**.

**Finishing.** If the clips came back at 720p, one upscale pass with Higgsfield `upscale_video`, `ugc` preset, on all three. One grain value and one sharpen value for the episode, kept for the series. Light grade only (lift the shadows a touch).

**End card (29.6–30.0 s, rising from 28.6 s).** `Tip of the Week · Ep 1: The edge of page one` over the full row 5 crop, the permission line, and the brand lockup you choose (`Hulk Marketing`, or `Hulk Marketing · part of Google Ranker Pro`). Hulk lime `#C6FA61` on `#121C17` if you pick Hulk for social; the receipt card itself stays navy with the orange underline. Add `Next week: Own your name` only once Ep 2 is cleared.

## What this video is

- **Concept.** Hassan stands at a wall monitor in his real office and explains one real client result in the order **"Here's what we did. Here's what Google shows now."** What we did comes only from the Golden Line work log (G7), shown as dated captures of the work itself: the live footer credit "Made with ❤ by Hulk Marketing Ltd" and the site's own lists of town and airport pages. What Google shows now: the airport searches average page one (5.3; 6.1 at 13% click-through; 7.1) and "kenilworth taxis" 6.7. The honest next job: 1,522 times shown across "taxi warwick", "warwick taxi" and "warwick taxis", averaging 10.7–12.6, the edge of page one.
- **Hook.** 16:9: Hassan already at the monitor, pen raised, turning to camera. 9:16: a 2 s stitch of the Golden Line owner's own approved V01 line, with `warwick airport taxi · 13% click-through` on screen by 0.8 s.
- **Why this brand.** Golden Line is the only client with a verified Hulk footer credit **and** an attributed Search Console screenshot, so "what we did" and "what Google shows" can both be proved on screen.
- **What the edit reveals.** The footer credit and the town and airport menus (dated captures), the date window, then the real rows: 20, 6, 7 and 4 (page one on average), then rows 5, 9 and 3 and the sum card `665 + 486 + 371 = 1,522 times shown · avg 10.7–12.6`. No causal verbs (made, drove, caused) and no growth: there is no comparison period.

| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v15_line2.m4a` | `v15_A-01` (both ratios) · second 7 | **G7:** "We built the site, with pages for the airports and the towns around Warwick." [ONLY WHAT THE WORK LOG CONFIRMS] | second 13 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v15_line3.m4a` | `v15_A-02` · second 1 | "Last three months, the airport searches average page one. Five point three, six point one, seven point one." | second 8 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v15_line4.m4a` | `v15_A-02` · second 8 | "And Kenilworth taxis: six point seven." | second 11 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v15_line5.m4a` | `v15_A-03` (both ratios) · second 1 | "The next job is the big one: taxi Warwick, and the ways people type it." | second 6 |
| `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v15_line6.m4a` | `v15_A-03` (both ratios) · second 6 | "Fifteen hundred and twenty-two times shown, averaging ten point seven to twelve point six. The edge of page one." | second 13 |

**9:16 stitch (no new recording):** 2 s from the Golden Line owner's own approved V01 clip (`grp_v01_A-04_*_9x16.mp4`, his line 6, Q3 "What's different now, day to day?"). **DRAFT FOR CLIENT APPROVAL:** we propose the exact 2 s excerpt (a complete phrase, never a sentence cut so its meaning changes) and he approves that excerpt in writing for V15. Until then it is `[APPROVED 2 s EXCERPT OF HIS V01 LINE 6]`. He says no numbers.

**Rules for the lines**
- Every number matches `assets/gsc/gsc_data.json`: rows 20, 6, 7 (5.3, 6.1, 7.1), row 4 (6.7), rows 5, 9, 3 (665 + 486 + 371 = 1,522, at 10.7, 12.6, 11.5). If Hassan rewords a line, the numbers stay exactly as they are.
- Offered for Hassan's approval in line 3: "the **three** airport searches average page one" (it names exactly the three rows shown). Keep the current wording if he prefers it.
- "Times shown", never "people saw" or "people searched". "Last three months", never "last quarter".
- No causal verbs (made, drove, caused), no "No.1", "first", "just hit", "growth". "Here's what Google shows now" is the plan's approved framing, kept as written.
- Each line is said at a natural pace, the way he'd say it to a client on the phone. If a line runs past its "must end by" second, shorten the words, not the pace.

**How to record a memo (send this to Hassan)**
- A quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a lounge or bedroom (not a kitchen or stairwell). No TV, radio, fan or music.
- Hold the phone about **30 cm** from your mouth, slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop.
- Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
- **One line per file:** three takes in the same file with a 2-second gap between them. We keep the best take, trimmed to the line plus 0.3 s, under the file name in the table.
- **Send us Hassan's raw memo; we send back `MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v15_lineN.m4a` (one take, line + 0.3 s). Attach only that file as @Audio**, never the raw three-take file.
- Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. **Not WhatsApp.**
- His accent is never described in any prompt. The memo carries the voice.

**Which memo goes where.** Each memo is the `@Audio` reference in its Seedance shot (it guides timbre and pace), and we lay the real memo in as the final track wherever sync allows. **If the generated voice doesn't sound like Hassan, the clip fails QC** (production_rules G.1). **Before pasting any Seedance prompt:** replace the quoted words with his approved words exactly, keeping the start second.

Vertical close-up: the presenter in the lower half of the frame, a closed-lip half-smile fading, eyes on the interviewer just past camera-left, plain soft wall above, camera holding.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated. Her moss-green cardigan stays exactly as in the reference.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
Fingers do not touch the face during speech.
She blinks naturally, glances away to think and takes a breath before a line.
Exactly one person visible. No extra people.
Filmed on a handheld documentary video camera in available light: natural colour with a restrained grade, fine even digital grain, soft highlight roll-off on bright windows, real depth of field with a gently soft background.
```

- **QC (pass/fail):** as N1-03_16x9, plus: **receipt space**, the upper third stays plain for all 14 s. *Fail → remake the anchor still with more headroom.*
- **Save as:** `grp_v15_N1-03_t1_9x16.mp4`

- **Captions:** his approved words only, word-timed, white with a soft shadow, Inter, two lines at most. 16:9 in the lower third (web autoplays muted); 9:16 in the band y 1300–1520.
- **Sound:** Seedance's native room tone and foley stay; his real memos are laid in wherever sync allows, checked frame by frame. **No music under A-01.** One optional sparse licensed bed under −20 LU from 13 s to the end; a soft tick on each underline; no trending or copyrighted audio.
